item.title: How to use Ollama to run AI models on your own computer
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: In the Ollama app on Mac, open Apps and turn on Claude. Claude Desktop then runs the model you pick in Ollama. Turn it off to go back to your old setup. Local models need no account or API key. Ollama's cloud models have a small free monthly allowance. Pro costs $20 a month and includes $60 of usage. Sources: Ollama docs: Quickstart, Ollama docs: CLI reference, Ollama: Download, Ollama blog: Transparent pricing, Ollama blog: Claude Desktop support, LLM Hardware: Ollama cheat sheet.

nf:hero.nf:alt: Ollama's black-and-white logo.

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use Ollama to run AI models on your own computer, step by step","dek":"Ollama downloads open models and runs them locally with one command. Here is how to install it, which commands matter and how much memory you need.","summary":"Ollama is a free app for Mac, Windows and Linux that runs open AI models on your own computer and needs no account for local use. It can also plug local models into Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex, and offers paid cloud models.","seo_title":"How to use Ollama to run AI models on your own computer","seo_description":"How to use Ollama: install it, run your first model with one command, manage models, check memory needs and connect it to Claude and Codex.","answer_summary":"Install Ollama from ollama.com/download, open a terminal and type ollama run gemma4:e2b. Ollama downloads the model and starts a chat on your own computer; type /bye to leave. Local models need no account or API key.","tags":["Ollama","Local AI","Open models","Guides","Gemma"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"How to use Ollama, in short: download it from ollama.com/download, open a terminal and type ollama run followed by a model name. Ollama downloads the model and starts a chat that runs on your own computer. It is available for macOS, Windows and Linux, and local models need no account and no API key.","sources":[{"name":"Ollama docs: Quickstart","url":"https://docs.ollama.com/quickstart"},{"name":"Ollama: Download","url":"https://ollama.com/download"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The appeal is privacy and control. A local model runs on your own hardware, so your prompts do not have to leave it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Ollama also sells cloud models, and it can connect models to tools such as Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex.","sources":[{"name":"Ollama docs: Quickstart","url":"https://docs.ollama.com/quickstart"},{"name":"Ollama blog: Transparent pricing","url":"https://ollama.com/blog/transparent-pricing"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to install Ollama","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Download it","text":"Go to ollama.com/download and pick macOS, Windows or Linux. On Linux the page gives a one-line install command that you paste into a terminal.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Linux install command","text":"curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Run the setup","text":"Open the app, or type ollama in a terminal and follow the prompts. During setup you either sign in to use cloud models or choose a local model.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"You can skip the sign-in if you only want local models. The docs say an account and API key are needed only for Ollama's cloud models.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Run your first model in Ollama","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Ollama's own quickstart uses gemma4:e2b, a small version of Gemma 4. The download is about 7.2 GB, and Ollama recommends about 8 GB of free graphics memory, or unified memory on a Mac. With less, Ollama falls back to system memory and answers get slower.","sources":[{"name":"Ollama docs: Quickstart","url":"https://docs.ollama.com/quickstart"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Command 1: Download and chat","text":"ollama run gemma4:e2b","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Chat and leave","text":"Type your question after the prompt and press Enter. Type /bye when you are done. To paste several lines as one message, start and end the block with three quote marks.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Command 2: Ask about an image","text":"ollama run gemma4 \"What's in this image? [path to your picture]\"","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Put a prompt right after the model name, as in the image example, to get a one-off answer without opening a chat.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"The Ollama commands you will actually use","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Ollama's CLI reference lists a short set of commands: ollama pull downloads a model without starting it, ollama ls lists downloaded models, ollama ps shows what is running, ollama stop unloads a model and ollama rm deletes it from disk.","sources":[{"name":"Ollama docs: CLI reference","url":"https://docs.ollama.com/cli.md"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Command 3: Clean up disk space","text":"ollama ls\nollama rm [model name]","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"LLM Hardware's cheat sheet adds a useful check: ollama ps shows how much of a model sits on the graphics card. Below 100 percent means part of it spilled to the processor, and speed can drop to roughly 1 to 5 tokens per second.","sources":[{"name":"LLM Hardware: Ollama cheat sheet","url":"https://llmhardware.io/guides/ollama-cheat-sheet"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Ollama only listens on your own computer by default. LLM Hardware notes that opening it to other devices means changing the OLLAMA_HOST setting, which exposes the service on your network, so only do that on a network you trust.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How much memory you need","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The same guide estimates graphics memory at the common 4-bit setting: about 6.8 GB for an 8 billion parameter model, about 10.4 GB for 14 billion, about 21 GB for 32 billion and about 44 GB for a 70 billion model. Longer conversations need more on top of that.","sources":[{"name":"LLM Hardware: Ollama cheat sheet","url":"https://llmhardware.io/guides/ollama-cheat-sheet"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"For most laptops that means small models. They are fine for summaries, rewriting and simple questions, but they are not as sharp as the big cloud assistants. Start small and move up only if your machine keeps up.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Connect Ollama to Claude, Codex and other apps","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"Claude Desktop","text":"In the Ollama app on a Mac, open Apps and turn on Claude. Ollama sets up the connection, and you choose the model in Ollama. Turn Claude off to restore your previous setup.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Command 4: Start a coding agent on a local model","text":"ollama launch claude","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Run that from your project folder. The quickstart says ollama launch also works with codex and opencode, and Ollama offers to install Claude Code or OpenCode if they are missing. Codex has to be installed first.","sources":[{"name":"Ollama docs: Quickstart","url":"https://docs.ollama.com/quickstart"},{"name":"Ollama docs: CLI reference","url":"https://docs.ollama.com/cli.md"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Ollama free plan and cloud prices","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Local use is free. For cloud models, Ollama's free plan includes a small monthly amount of usage on a set of starter models. Pro costs $20 a month with $60 of usage included, Max costs $100 a month with $300, and Team starts at $500 a month. Usage is billed per token, and unused amounts do not roll over.","sources":[{"name":"Ollama blog: Transparent pricing","url":"https://ollama.com/blog/transparent-pricing"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Ollama is the easiest way to try local AI, but it is a terminal tool at heart. If you never want to type a command, it will feel bare. If you care about keeping your data on your own machine, it is the first thing to install.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Adobe Firefly, and Firefly in Photoshop
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Open firefly.adobe.com, choose Image, then Generate image. The Model menu lists Adobe and partner models. Firefly Image 4 gives four variations. Image 5 gives one. In Photoshop, select an area, click Generative Fill, type what you want and press Generate. Leave the prompt blank to fill the spot from the pixels around it. Sources: Adobe Help: Generate images from text descriptions in Firefly, Adobe Help: Generative credits FAQ, Adobe: Firefly plans, Adobe Help: Edit images with Generative Fill in Photoshop, The Next Web: Adobe's Firefly AI Assistant.

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use Adobe Firefly: images, Generative Fill in Photoshop and credits explained","dek":"Adobe's AI makes images and video from a prompt and edits photos inside Photoshop. Here is how to get a good first image and how far the free plan goes.","summary":"Adobe Firefly generates images, video and audio from text on the web and powers Generative Fill in Photoshop. The free plan gives limited daily generations, and paid plans start at $9.99 a month for 2,000 credits.","seo_title":"How to use Adobe Firefly (and Firefly in Photoshop)","seo_description":"How to use Adobe Firefly step by step: pick a model, write the prompt, use Generative Fill in Photoshop and see what each plan's credits buy.","answer_summary":"Go to firefly.adobe.com, choose Image and then Generate image, pick a model, set the aspect ratio, describe the picture and click Generate. In Photoshop, select an area, click Generative Fill, type a prompt or leave it blank, and click Generate.","tags":["Adobe Firefly","Photoshop","Generative Fill","Guides","AI images"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"How to use Adobe Firefly, in short: open the Firefly website, choose Image and then Generate image, pick a model, describe the picture and click Generate. The same AI also works inside Photoshop as Generative Fill, where you select part of a photo and tell it what to add, remove or change.","sources":[{"name":"Adobe Help: Generate images from text descriptions in Firefly","url":"https://helpx.adobe.com/firefly/web/work-with-images/generate-images/generate-images-from-text-descriptions.html"},{"name":"Adobe Help: Edit images with Generative Fill in Photoshop","url":"https://helpx.adobe.com/photoshop/desktop/create-open-import-images/create-images/edit-images-with-generative-fill.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Firefly is no longer only Adobe's own model. The Model menu lists Adobe models such as Firefly Image 4, Image 4 Ultra and Image 5 next to partner models, and Adobe's credits FAQ names Google, OpenAI, ElevenLabs and Topaz among the partners. Since June 2026 Adobe has also tested a Firefly AI Assistant, a chat sidebar inside Photoshop, Premiere and Illustrator that takes plain requests, according to The Next Web.","sources":[{"name":"Adobe Help: Generate images from text descriptions in Firefly","url":"https://helpx.adobe.com/firefly/web/work-with-images/generate-images/generate-images-from-text-descriptions.html"},{"name":"Adobe Help: Generative credits FAQ","url":"https://helpx.adobe.com/firefly/using/generative-credits-faq.html"},{"name":"The Next Web: Adobe's Firefly AI Assistant","url":"https://thenextweb.com/news/adobe-ai-week-firefly-agent-disney-semrush-genstudio-linkedin"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use Adobe Firefly on the web","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Open Generate image","text":"Go to firefly.adobe.com, select Image in the left panel and then Generate image.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Choose a model","text":"Under General settings, open the Model dropdown. Settings change with the model. Firefly Image 4 returns four variations per prompt, while Image 4 Ultra and Image 5 return one image each.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Set the shape and the look","text":"Pick an aspect ratio. Under Content type choose Photo or Art, or leave it on auto. The Visual intensity slider controls how strong the image's visual attributes are.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Write the prompt","text":"Type the description in the Prompt field. Adobe's help page asks for simple, direct language and at least three words. Name the subject, where it is and the light you want.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: A clean product photo","text":"A ceramic coffee mug on a wooden kitchen table, morning light from a window on the left, soft shadows, close-up","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: A flat illustration","text":"Flat illustration of a small bookshop on a rainy street at night, warm light in the windows, simple shapes, [your brand colors]","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Generate and download","text":"Click Generate. Switch to list view to download all variations at once. In that view, Use settings starts a new set with the same settings and Generate more reruns the same prompt. View all above the prompt bar opens your full generation history.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Two optional settings do most of the work for a consistent look. Upload a picture under Composition to keep its outline and depth, or under Styles to copy its visual style, and use the Strength slider to decide how closely Firefly follows it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Next to the Generate button, Prompt features can turn on Prompt enhancement, which rewrites your prompt automatically. Adobe lists it for Firefly Image 4 and Image 4 Ultra.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use Firefly in Photoshop with Generative Fill","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Generative Fill is Firefly inside Photoshop on the desktop. Adobe describes it as a non-destructive edit, so the original pixels stay underneath the result.","sources":[{"name":"Adobe Help: Edit images with Generative Fill in Photoshop","url":"https://helpx.adobe.com/photoshop/desktop/create-open-import-images/create-images/edit-images-with-generative-fill.html"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Open an image","text":"Choose File, then Open, and load the photo.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Select the area","text":"Use a selection tool, for example the Selection Brush, to mark the part you want to change.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Pick a model and prompt","text":"Select Generative Fill. In the Contextual Task Bar, open the model picker. Adobe lists Firefly Fill and Expand, Firefly Image 5 and Firefly Image 1, plus partner models such as FLUX.2 pro and Gemini with Nano Banana. Type what should appear in the selection.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Generate and choose","text":"Click Generate, then pick the variation you like in the Properties panel.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"To remove something, select it and leave the prompt blank. Photoshop then fills the selection from the surrounding pixels instead of adding a new object.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Adobe Firefly free plan, prices and credits","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Adobe's plans page describes the free plan as limited free daily generations for images and video, with limited access to top models from Adobe, Google, OpenAI and others. Adobe does not publish a fixed number for it.","sources":[{"name":"Adobe: Firefly plans","url":"https://www.adobe.com/products/firefly/plans.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Firefly Standard costs $9.99 a month for 2,000 credits, which Adobe says is up to 400 images or 20 five-second videos. Firefly Pro is $19.99 a month for 4,000 credits, and Pro Plus is $49.99 a month for 10,000 credits, both with lower prices for the first six months at the time of writing.","sources":[{"name":"Adobe: Firefly plans","url":"https://www.adobe.com/products/firefly/plans.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Credits are spent per generation. Adobe's FAQ lists Firefly Image 5 at 10 credits and Image 4 Ultra at 20. Video costs far more: Generate Video uses 100 credits per second at 1080p, 50 at 720p and 20 at 540p. Partner models count as premium, and their price depends on the model.","sources":[{"name":"Adobe Help: Generative credits FAQ","url":"https://helpx.adobe.com/firefly/using/generative-credits-faq.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Standard features, such as Generative Fill with Firefly models, are unlimited and do not use credits on the Firefly Standard, Pro, Pro Plus and Premium plans and on Creative Cloud Pro, according to the FAQ. Creative Cloud Standard includes only 25 credits a month. Credits do not roll over, and failed generations are usually refunded within minutes.","sources":[{"name":"Adobe Help: Generative credits FAQ","url":"https://helpx.adobe.com/firefly/using/generative-credits-faq.html"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Firefly is bad at","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The credit system is the main trap. Premium models and video burn through a monthly allowance quickly, and unused credits vanish at the reset. Before a big project, check the model's cost and your balance in the Account Menu. Partner models also come and go: Adobe keeps a list of deprecated partner models, so a model you rely on today may be gone later.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Firefly makes the most sense if you already work in Photoshop, because Generative Fill fixes real photos in place. For one-off pictures with no editing after, the free daily generations are a fair way to test it before paying.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Google AI Studio for free
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Google says AI Studio stays free of charge unless you link a paid API key. Free use covers certain models with rate limits. Some models are marked Paid. Sources: Google AI for Developers: Google AI Studio quickstart, Google AI for Developers: Build apps in Google AI Studio, Google AI for Developers: Billing, Google Blog: Google AI Studio at I/O 2026, NYU IT: Google AI Studio, Google AI Developers Forum: Gemini 4 Argon in AI Studio.
item.category: Google AI for Developers: Google AI Studio quickstart
Google AI for Developers: Build apps in Google AI Studio
Google Blog: Google AI Studio at I/O 2026
Google AI Developers Forum: Gemini 4 Argon in AI Studio

nf:hero.nf:alt: Google AI Studio promotional graphic on a dark background.

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use Google AI Studio for free: prompts, settings and Build mode","dek":"Google's browser playground for Gemini costs nothing until you link a paid API key. Here is how to test prompts, set system instructions and build a first app.","summary":"Google AI Studio is a free web tool for trying Gemini models, writing system instructions and turning a working prompt into code. Its Build mode can also create and deploy a small web or Android app from a description.","seo_title":"How to use Google AI Studio for free: a step-by-step guide","seo_description":"How to use Google AI Studio for free: test Gemini prompts, set system instructions, get code and build an app in Build mode, step by step.","answer_summary":"Open aistudio.google.com, start a chat prompt in the Playground, set System Instructions under Run settings and click Run. AI Studio is free unless you link a paid API key, and Build mode at aistudio.google.com/apps turns a description into an app.","tags":["Google AI Studio","Gemini","Gemini API","Guides","Vibe coding"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"How to use Google AI Studio, in short: open aistudio.google.com, type a prompt in the Playground, change how the model behaves under Run settings, and click Get code when the result is right. Google describes AI Studio as the place to try its models and experiment with prompts before building with the Gemini API.","sources":[{"name":"Google AI for Developers: Google AI Studio quickstart","url":"https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/ai-studio-quickstart"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"It is not the Gemini app. The Gemini app is a chat assistant. AI Studio is a workbench: you pick the model, write the rules it follows, upload files, adjust settings such as temperature and copy the exact setup into your own code. NYU's IT department, which offers it to staff and students, calls it a web environment for rapid prototyping with Gemini models.","sources":[{"name":"Google AI for Developers: Google AI Studio quickstart","url":"https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/ai-studio-quickstart"},{"name":"NYU IT: Google AI Studio","url":"https://www.nyu.edu/life/information-technology/artificial-intelligence-at-nyu/generative-ai-services/ai-studio.html"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Google AI Studio free tier and paid models","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"For most people it is free. Google's billing documentation says AI Studio usage remains free of charge unless you link a paid API key for paid features. New accounts start on the Free Tier, which gives access to certain models, each with its own rate limits. Which models are included depends on the model, and Google keeps that list on its pricing page.","sources":[{"name":"Google AI for Developers: Billing","url":"https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/billing"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Some models are paid only. In Google's developer forum, users point out that Gemini 4 Argon carries a Paid label in AI Studio and needs either a Google AI subscription or an API key from a project with billing turned on. If you see that label, pick another model to stay free.","sources":[{"name":"Google AI Developers Forum: Gemini 4 Argon in AI Studio","url":"https://discuss.ai.google.dev/t/inquiry-about-gemini-4-argon-in-ai-studio-is-the-web-ui-free-to-use-and-why-is-setting-up-api-billing-required/197458"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Do not paste anything private while you are on the free tier. Google's billing page says paid use is how you make sure prompts and responses are not used to improve Google products, and NYU's guide says the same about the paid tier. Treat free use as public test data.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use Google AI Studio: your first prompt","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Open the Playground","text":"Go to aistudio.google.com. The Playground opens with a new chat prompt by default.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Open Run settings","text":"Click Run settings, the tune icon at the top right. This panel holds the model parameters, the safety settings and tools such as structured output, function calling, code execution and grounding.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Write a system instruction","text":"Find the System Instructions field and describe the role and rules you want. Google's own example turns the model into an alien living on Europa. Something practical works better for daily use.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: A tutor that keeps it short","text":"You are a patient tutor. Answer in under 3 short paragraphs, use plain words and end with one question that checks I understood.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Ask and run","text":"Type your message in the box at the bottom and click Run. You can change the system instruction in the middle of a chat and run the same question again to compare answers. Google's quickstart uses exactly this to refine a bot's tone and length.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Every message in the chat is sent with the next one, so long conversations grow and can hit the model's token limit. Start a new prompt when you change topic.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Click Get code","text":"When the answers look right, click Get code. AI Studio gives you the same prompt, model and settings as code in your preferred language for the Gemini API. You can also save the prompt and share it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Build an app in Google AI Studio","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Build mode is where AI Studio becomes a vibe coding tool. You describe an app in plain words and an agent writes it. Web apps get a React front end and a Node.js server by default, and the docs say AI Studio can also build native Android apps in Kotlin.","sources":[{"name":"Google AI for Developers: Build apps in Google AI Studio","url":"https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/aistudio-build-mode"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Open Build mode","text":"Go to aistudio.google.com/apps. Type a description in the prompt box. You can add AI Chips, for example for image generation or Google Maps data, or click I'm Feeling Lucky to have Gemini suggest an idea.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: A small app to start with","text":"Build a simple web app where I paste a recipe and it turns it into a shopping list grouped by store section. Keep the design clean and make it work on a phone.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Watch the preview","text":"After you run the prompt, the generated files appear with a live preview on the right. The Code tab shows the code itself.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Fix it one change at a time","text":"Ask for changes in the chat panel, or use annotation mode: highlight part of the screen and describe what should change. You can also edit the code directly in the Code tab.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Keep or deploy it","text":"Download the project as a ZIP, sync it to GitHub, or deploy it to Cloud Run. Apps are private until you share them.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Deploying does not have to cost money at first. Google said at I/O 2026 that new builders can deploy their first two apps to Google Cloud at no cost and without a credit card. After that, Cloud Run pricing may apply, and when other people use a shared app its API calls count toward your limits.","sources":[{"name":"Google AI for Developers: Build apps in Google AI Studio","url":"https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/aistudio-build-mode"},{"name":"Google Blog: Google AI Studio at I/O 2026","url":"https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/google-ai-studio-io-2026/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Google AI Studio is bad at","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"AI Studio is built for testing, not for daily chatting. The free tier rate limits are tight once several people use one app, and NYU's guide says caching and batching are paid features. Build mode also has gaps the docs admit: there is no built-in storage yet and no real-time editing with teammates, so a shared GitHub repository is the workaround.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If a shared app shows a 403 Access Restricted error, Google's docs suggest turning off privacy extensions such as Privacy Badger, or asking the agent to fix the build and sharing again.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"When to pay","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"To move a project to the paid tier, open the API keys or Projects page in AI Studio and click Set up billing. Depending on your account you may be asked to prepay at least $5. Tiers then go up automatically once you meet the spending criteria, with Tier 1 capped at $250.","sources":[{"name":"Google AI for Developers: Billing","url":"https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/billing"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"For learning, testing prompts and building a first app, the free tier is enough. Pay when you need a paid-only model, higher limits for real users or the promise that your prompts stay out of Google's product training.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Wispr Flow to type with your voice
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: The free plan covers 2,000 words a week on Mac and Windows. After that it slows down until Sunday. Pro is $15 a month or $144 a year for unlimited dictation. Click where you want the text, hold Fn on a Mac (Ctrl and Win on Windows), speak, then let go. Double-tap the shortcut to dictate hands-free. Sources: Wispr Flow Help Center: What is Wispr Flow?, Wispr Flow Help Center: Setup guide, Wispr Flow Help Center: Plans, Wispr Flow Help Center: Dictionary, Wispr Flow Help Center: Command Mode, Spokenly: Wispr Flow review, TechCrunch, SiliconANGLE.

Wispr Flow Help Center: Setup guide

nf:hero.nf:alt: How to use Wispr Flow to type with your voice

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use Wispr Flow on Mac and Windows: voice typing with AI, step by step","dek":"Wispr Flow turns speech into clean text in any app. Here is how to set it up, the shortcuts that matter, what the free plan covers and where it falls short.","summary":"Wispr Flow is an AI dictation app that types what you say into any text field on Mac, Windows, iPhone and Android, removing filler words and adding punctuation. The free plan gives 2,000 words a week on desktop; Pro costs $15 a month or $144 a year.","seo_title":"How to use Wispr Flow on Mac and Windows (free plan explained)","seo_description":"How to use Wispr Flow: setup, the Fn and Ctrl+Win shortcuts, hands-free mode, Dictionary, Command Mode, and what the free 2,000 words a week get you.","answer_summary":"Install Wispr Flow, sign in, allow the microphone (and Accessibility on Mac), then click into any text box, hold Fn on a Mac or your chosen shortcut on Windows, speak and release. The text appears where your cursor is.","tags":["Wispr Flow","Voice typing","Dictation","AI tools","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"How to use Wispr Flow, in short: put your cursor where you want text, hold one shortcut key, talk, and let go. Flow turns what you said into cleaned up text and drops it into whatever app you are in, according to Wispr's help center. It removes filler words, adds punctuation and handles it when you correct yourself mid-sentence. It runs on Mac, Windows, iPhone and Android, and it needs an internet connection because transcription happens in the cloud.","sources":[{"name":"Wispr Flow Help Center: What is Wispr Flow?","url":"https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/2772472373-what-is-flow"},{"name":"Spokenly: Wispr Flow review","url":"https://spokenly.app/blog/wispr-flow-review"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"It is not a niche tool anymore. Wispr AI raised $280 million in August 2026 at a $2 billion valuation, and the company says users have written more than 60 billion words with Flow, according to SiliconANGLE. This guide covers setup, the shortcuts worth learning, the free plan and the honest downsides.","sources":[{"name":"SiliconANGLE","url":"https://siliconangle.com/2026/08/17/wispr-raises-280m-to-power-up-natural-speech-to-text-using-ai/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Wispr Flow free plan and prices","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The free plan gives you 2,000 words a week on Mac and Windows, with a hard cap of 5,000. Past 2,000, Flow slows down; at the cap, dictation stops until the weekly reset at midnight Pacific time on Sunday. iPhone and Android share a separate weekly allowance, according to Wispr's plans page.","sources":[{"name":"Wispr Flow Help Center: Plans","url":"https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/9559327591"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Pro costs $15 a month or $144 a year, which works out to about $12 a month, and removes the word limit. A default trial lasts 14 days, and students with a recognized .edu address can get longer trials. Team plans start at $23 per user per month. Prices outside the US are set in local currency, so they may differ.","sources":[{"name":"Wispr Flow Help Center: Plans","url":"https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/9559327591"},{"name":"Spokenly: Wispr Flow review","url":"https://spokenly.app/blog/wispr-flow-review"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Two thousand words is roughly a handful of long emails. Use the free week to test whether you actually dictate every day before you pay for unlimited.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to set up Wispr Flow on Mac and Windows","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Download and open Flow","text":"Get the app from wisprflow.ai/download. On a Mac, move it to Applications and open it; a menu bar icon shows it is running. On Windows, run the installer and open Flow from the Start menu; it lives in the system tray.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Sign in","text":"Click Sign in via browser and use Google, Apple, Microsoft, SSO or email. If your company uses SSO, check with IT first instead of making a separate account.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Allow the microphone","text":"Flow asks for microphone access on both systems, plus Accessibility on a Mac so it can type into other apps. If you clicked deny, turn it on under System Settings, Privacy and Security on a Mac, or Settings, Privacy and Security, Microphone on Windows. Use Test your microphone to check that it hears you.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Pick your shortcut and languages","text":"On a Mac with an fn key, the default is fn. On a Mac without one, it is Ctrl and Option. On Windows the help center lists Ctrl and Win as the default, and you can change it with Edit shortcut. Pick your languages or leave automatic detection on; Flow supports more than 100 languages and you can mix them in one sentence.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Do your first dictation","text":"Click into any text box, an email, a chat, a doc. Press and hold your shortcut, speak normally, then release. On desktop the text appears after you let go, not word by word as you talk.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Go hands-free for long text","text":"Double-tap your shortcut to start hands-free dictation, so you do not have to hold the key for a long message.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Make Wispr Flow spell your words right","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The Dictionary is where you teach Flow names, product terms and jargon. On Mac or Windows, open Dictionary in the left sidebar, click Add new, type the word and click Add word. Then dictate a sentence with it to check. If Flow keeps writing the same wrong spelling, add a correction: turn on Correct a misspelling and enter the wrong version Flow produces.","sources":[{"name":"Wispr Flow Help Center: Dictionary","url":"https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/4052411709"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"On desktop Flow can also learn words by itself when the auto-learn setting is on and you fix dictated text. It skips everyday words, numbers, web addresses and very famous names. You can import up to 1,000 entries from a file on Mac and Windows.","sources":[{"name":"Wispr Flow Help Center: Dictionary","url":"https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/4052411709"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Edit text by voice with Command Mode","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Command Mode lets you speak an instruction instead of text: edit what you wrote, draft a reply or run a web search. It is off by default; turn it on under Settings, Experimental. The default shortcut is Fn and Ctrl on a Mac and Ctrl, Win and Alt on Windows. The help center ties it to Pro, active trials and enterprise plans.","sources":[{"name":"Wispr Flow Help Center: Command Mode","url":"https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/4816967992-how-to-use-command-mode"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Command 1: Tighten a message","text":"Make this shorter and friendlier, and keep the dates.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Command 2: Fix the tone","text":"Rewrite this so it sounds professional, not annoyed.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Command 3: Draft a reply","text":"Write a short reply that says yes to Thursday and asks for the agenda.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Hold the Command Mode shortcut, say the instruction with no wake word, and release. Press Esc to cancel. Asking it to build a website or an app only gives you drafted text, not a working app, the help center notes.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Wispr Flow is bad at","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"There is no offline mode: everything goes through the cloud, so a bad connection means no dictation. A May 2026 review by Spokenly, which makes a rival app, also says the AI cleanup sometimes over-edits what you said, real-world delay is about one to two seconds, and data sharing for model training is on unless you opt out. Wispr's onboarding asks for your data preference, so read that screen instead of clicking through.","sources":[{"name":"Wispr Flow Help Center: What is Wispr Flow?","url":"https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/2772472373-what-is-flow"},{"name":"Wispr Flow Help Center: Setup guide","url":"https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/3152211871-setup-guide"},{"name":"Spokenly: Wispr Flow review","url":"https://spokenly.app/blog/wispr-flow-review"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Flow is worth it if you write a lot of email, chat and notes and talk faster than you type. If you mostly write code, numbers or work offline, the free week will show you quickly that it is not your tool.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Google's new Gemini 4 Hydrogen is here, and free users get it
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen on November 12 as the replacement for Gemini 3.8 Flash. Google says it finishes tasks 2.5 times as fast as Flash and calls it the daily driver of the Gemini 4 family. Hydrogen now powers Google Search for all users worldwide, at no cost. Google says it handles typos and multi-part questions better. In the Gemini app, free users get it automatically when a prompt fits. Google says Hydrogen makes more than 5 times fewer fabricated claims than Gemini 3.8 Flash. Sources: VentureBeat, MakeUseOf, Digital Trends, Chrome Unboxed.

nf:hero.nf:alt: Google's promotional artwork announcing the Gemini 4 Hydrogen model.

item.nf:article: {"headline":"Google releases Gemini 4 Hydrogen and puts it in Search for all users","dek":"The faster model replaces Gemini 3.8 Flash in Search and the Gemini app, with a higher API price for developers.","summary":"Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen on November 12, 2026, as the successor to Gemini 3.8 Flash and made it the model behind Google Search for all users. Google says it completes tasks 2.5 times as fast as Flash, and developers pay $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens.","seo_title":"Gemini 4 Hydrogen: Google's Flash successor, price and access","seo_description":"Google's Gemini 4 Hydrogen replaces Gemini 3.8 Flash. Who gets it in Search and the Gemini app, what it costs developers and what Google claims.","answer_summary":"Gemini 4 Hydrogen is free in Google Search for all users and reaches free Gemini app users automatically when a prompt fits; developers pay $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens.","tags":["Google","Gemini","Gemini 4 Hydrogen","Google Search","AI models"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen on November 12, 2026, a faster model in the Gemini 4 family that takes over from Gemini 3.8 Flash. According to VentureBeat and Digital Trends, the model is rolling out at once across Google Search, the Gemini app, Google AI Studio, the Gemini API and Google's business products.","sources":[{"name":"VentureBeat","url":"https://venturebeat.com/technology/google-launches-gemini-4-hydrogen-a-faster-smarter-pricier-flash-successor"},{"name":"Digital Trends","url":"https://www.digitaltrends.com/cool-tech/googles-next-gen-gemini-4-hydrogen-ai-model-is-here-touting-faster-intelligence-for-all/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Digital Trends reported that Google describes Hydrogen as its daily driver for agent work, built for speed and efficiency, while the heavier Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon models handle long, deep reasoning. Hydrogen arrives a few weeks after those two models.","sources":[{"name":"Digital Trends","url":"https://www.digitaltrends.com/cool-tech/googles-next-gen-gemini-4-hydrogen-ai-model-is-here-touting-faster-intelligence-for-all/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Who gets it","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Hydrogen now powers Google Search for all users worldwide, according to Digital Trends and Chrome Unboxed, and MakeUseOf noted that it is free to use there. Google says the model understands multi-part questions, typos and very specific requests better, gives answers that are easier to scan and shows a wider range of links in results.","sources":[{"name":"MakeUseOf","url":"https://www.makeuseof.com/gemini-4-hydrogen-rolls-out/"},{"name":"Digital Trends","url":"https://www.digitaltrends.com/cool-tech/googles-next-gen-gemini-4-hydrogen-ai-model-is-here-touting-faster-intelligence-for-all/"},{"name":"Chrome Unboxed","url":"https://chromeunboxed.com/gemini-4-hydrogen-is-here-with-frontier-level-speed-for-search-and-the-gemini-app/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"In the Gemini app, Hydrogen appears in the model picker. Free users are routed to it automatically when the app judges that a prompt calls for it. Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers also get it in Google Sheets, where Google says financial models are built more than 30 percent faster, and in the Antigravity coding tool.","sources":[{"name":"MakeUseOf","url":"https://www.makeuseof.com/gemini-4-hydrogen-rolls-out/"},{"name":"Chrome Unboxed","url":"https://chromeunboxed.com/gemini-4-hydrogen-is-here-with-frontier-level-speed-for-search-and-the-gemini-app/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Developers can use it in Google AI Studio, Android Studio and the Gemini API, and Google Cloud lists the model as generally available, according to VentureBeat. The context window is about 1 million tokens, and the model accepts text, images, audio and video as input.","sources":[{"name":"VentureBeat","url":"https://venturebeat.com/technology/google-launches-gemini-4-hydrogen-a-faster-smarter-pricier-flash-successor"},{"name":"Chrome Unboxed","url":"https://chromeunboxed.com/gemini-4-hydrogen-is-here-with-frontier-level-speed-for-search-and-the-gemini-app/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Google claims","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Google says Hydrogen completes tasks 2.5 times as fast as Gemini 3.8 Flash. At its default high reasoning setting, it scored 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, VentureBeat reported, compared with 31 for Flash and one point above Gemini 4 Argon. At the new xhigh setting it reached 54.","sources":[{"name":"VentureBeat","url":"https://venturebeat.com/technology/google-launches-gemini-4-hydrogen-a-faster-smarter-pricier-flash-successor"},{"name":"MakeUseOf","url":"https://www.makeuseof.com/gemini-4-hydrogen-rolls-out/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"On Terminal-Bench 4.1, Google's own comparison shows Hydrogen completing 57 percent of tasks, against 18.2 percent for Flash and 63.9 percent for Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 5.5. Digital Trends reported that Google places Hydrogen ahead of OpenAI's GPT 6.1 Terra and Claude Sonnet 5.5 on knowledge tests, but slightly behind in science, math and computer use.","sources":[{"name":"VentureBeat","url":"https://venturebeat.com/technology/google-launches-gemini-4-hydrogen-a-faster-smarter-pricier-flash-successor"},{"name":"Digital Trends","url":"https://www.digitaltrends.com/cool-tech/googles-next-gen-gemini-4-hydrogen-ai-model-is-here-touting-faster-intelligence-for-all/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Google also made safety claims. According to Digital Trends and MakeUseOf, the company says Hydrogen makes more than five times fewer fabricated claims than Flash, reduces overreach in agent tasks by up to 81 percent and is up to twice as unlikely to get around permission limits when a task is blocked. These figures come from Google and have not been checked independently.","sources":[{"name":"MakeUseOf","url":"https://www.makeuseof.com/gemini-4-hydrogen-rolls-out/"},{"name":"Digital Trends","url":"https://www.digitaltrends.com/cool-tech/googles-next-gen-gemini-4-hydrogen-ai-model-is-here-touting-faster-intelligence-for-all/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What developers pay","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The standard API price is $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens, including reasoning tokens. VentureBeat reported that this matches the standard Flash pricing scheduled from January 1, 2027, and is twice the introductory Flash rate that runs through December 31, 2026. Batch and Flex requests cost half the standard rate.","sources":[{"name":"VentureBeat","url":"https://venturebeat.com/technology/google-launches-gemini-4-hydrogen-a-faster-smarter-pricier-flash-successor"},{"name":"Chrome Unboxed","url":"https://chromeunboxed.com/gemini-4-hydrogen-is-here-with-frontier-level-speed-for-search-and-the-gemini-app/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Box, which tested the model early, reported that accuracy on its complex work evaluation rose from 74 percent with Flash to 79 percent with Hydrogen, VentureBeat said, with tasks taking less than half as long.","sources":[{"name":"VentureBeat","url":"https://venturebeat.com/technology/google-launches-gemini-4-hydrogen-a-faster-smarter-pricier-flash-successor"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"For most people the change is invisible but large: the model answering their Google searches has been replaced without any action on their part. The higher developer price suggests Google is betting that speed and fewer errors matter more to businesses than the cheapest possible rate.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"The next thing to watch is whether independent testers confirm Google's claims about fewer fabricated answers, since Hydrogen now writes the AI answers in Google Search for all users.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Lovable to build an app without writing code
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: The free plan gives 5 build credits a day, up to 30 a month. A color change costs about 0.50 credits. A landing page with images costs about 2. Type your idea in the prompt box with Build selected. The first version takes a few minutes. Chat sits on the left, a live preview on the right. Use the preview toolbar to pick one element and describe the change. It is cheaper than a new full prompt. Sources: Lovable Docs: Quick start, Lovable Docs: Plans and credits, Lovable Docs: Subscription plans, Lovable Docs: Prompting best practices, AppLaunchpad: Lovable review, TechCrunch.

nf:hero.nf:alt: How to use Lovable to build an app without writing code

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use Lovable to build an app without coding, and what the free plan gets you","dek":"Lovable turns a written description into a working web app. Here is how credits work, the steps to a first published app, and prompts to copy.","summary":"Lovable is an AI app builder that writes a working web app from a plain description, and the free plan includes 5 build credits a day, up to 30 a month. This guide covers credits and plans, the steps from first prompt to a published app, Plan mode, and prompts that waste fewer credits.","seo_title":"How to use Lovable to build an app without coding (free plan)","seo_description":"How to use Lovable: free credits and plans, the steps from first prompt to a published app, Plan mode, and prompts to copy that save credits.","answer_summary":"Sign up at Lovable, type what you want in the prompt box with Build mode selected, check the preview, ask for one change at a time and click Publish. The free plan gives 5 build credits a day, capped at 30 a month.","tags":["Lovable","AI app builder","Vibe coding","No code","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"How to use Lovable, in short: describe the app you want in plain words, let it build a first version, fix it one change at a time and click Publish. Lovable is an AI app builder from Stockholm that grew out of GPT Engineer, an open source tool built by its CEO Anton Osika. Lovable says a first app takes about ten minutes and needs nothing installed.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Quick start","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/introduction/getting-started"},{"name":"TechCrunch","url":"https://techcrunch.com/2025/11/10/lovable-says-its-nearing-8-million-users-as-the-year-old-ai-coding-startup-eyes-more-corporate-employees"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The catch is credits. Every build costs some, the free plan gets only a few a day, and an October 2026 review says vague prompts and repeated fixes burn through them quickly. This guide covers what you get for free, the steps to a first published app, and prompts that keep the cost down.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Plans and credits","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/introduction/plans-and-credits"},{"name":"AppLaunchpad: Lovable review","url":"https://theapplaunchpad.com/blog/lovable-review/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Lovable free plan, credits and prices","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The free plan includes 5 build credits a day, up to 30 a month. Once you hit 30, daily credits stop for the rest of the calendar month and come back on the 1st. Daily credits refresh at midnight UTC and do not roll over. Free users also get small monthly grants for Lovable Cloud, its backend, and for AI features inside the apps they build.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Plans and credits","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/introduction/plans-and-credits"},{"name":"Lovable Docs: Subscription plans","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/introduction/subscription-plans"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Build mode is priced by the work done. Lovable's own examples: a color change costs about 0.50 credits, removing a footer about 0.90, adding user login about 1.20 and a landing page with images about 2.00. Plan mode, where Lovable thinks with you before writing code, costs 1 credit per message. If you stop a build, you pay only for the work it finished.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Plans and credits","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/introduction/plans-and-credits"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Pro starts at $25 a month for 100 credits, plus the 5 daily build credits with no monthly cap. It adds code editing and download, custom domains, removal of the Edit with Lovable badge and rollover of unused monthly credits. Business starts at $50 a month and adds team features such as single sign-on and role-based access. Students and teachers can get 50 percent off Pro for up to 12 months.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Subscription plans","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/introduction/subscription-plans"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"On the free plan you cannot edit or download the code and cannot use your own domain, but Git sync with GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket is included. Publishing is free on every plan.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Subscription plans","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/introduction/subscription-plans"},{"name":"Lovable Docs: Quick start","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/introduction/getting-started"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use Lovable: your first app, step by step","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Create an account","text":"Sign up with email, Google, GitHub or Apple. You can also type your idea on the homepage first; Lovable keeps the prompt and asks you to sign up when you submit it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Describe your app in Build mode","text":"Type in the prompt box with Build selected in the mode picker. Any language works. Be concrete: what the app is, who it is for and which sections or screens it needs. You can also attach a sketch, a design or a screenshot as a visual reference, start from a template, or build from a link.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Watch the first version appear","text":"The first build takes a few minutes. The editor has the project chat on the left and a live preview on the right.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Change one thing at a time","text":"Ask for a single change, then check the preview before the next one. Every change is saved as a version you can restore, so a bad edit does not break the app for good.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Point at what you want changed","text":"For small fixes, use the preview toolbar to select an element and describe the change. For text, use Edit text inline and type straight onto the page. Lovable's own docs recommend this over writing a new prompt for small fixes.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Test it on a phone screen","text":"Click every button and link, then use the device toggle to switch to Mobile view. Most people will open your link on a phone.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"7. Publish","text":"Click Publish in the top right. Lovable suggests a lovable.app address that you can edit. The live site is a snapshot: later edits show up in the preview right away, but reach the live site only when you click Publish again and choose Publish changes.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Lovable prompts that save credits","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Lovable's prompting guide suggests building in a fixed order: the foundation (the product, the audience and the one key action), then the design direction, then one component at a time with real text, and finally a clear limit on what each change may touch. It also suggests saving your design rules in the project instructions so they carry across prompts.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Prompting best practices","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-one"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: The foundation","text":"Build a one-page website for [product], made for [audience]. The one thing visitors should do is [key action, for example book a table]. Sections: [list of sections]. No login or database yet.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Plan before building (use Plan mode)","text":"I want to add [feature] to this app. [Describe how it should work in two or three sentences.] Ask me any questions you need in order to fully understand what I want from this feature and how I envision it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: A scoped change","text":"Only change the [page or section name]. [Describe the change.] Keep the existing styling and leave the rest of the app unchanged.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: A clear design direction","text":"Use a [calm, bold or premium] design: [colors], [type of fonts], rounded corners and generous spacing. Apply it to the whole site without changing any text or layout.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Use real headlines and button text instead of placeholder text. The docs say placeholder copy hides layout problems that real words reveal. Specific words work better than vague ones: \"bold, saturated colors\" beats \"colorful\", and \"replace\" or \"adjust\" beats \"make this better\".","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Lovable is bad at","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"An AppLaunchpad review published on October 20, 2026 called Lovable one of the strongest tools for turning an idea into a working first version quickly. It also named credit burn as a major weakness, said some users need several prompts to fix a single bug, and said bigger, more complex projects still need manual fixing. Its advice: for a real production app, knowledge of React and backend code becomes much more valuable.","sources":[{"name":"AppLaunchpad: Lovable review","url":"https://theapplaunchpad.com/blog/lovable-review/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"That matches how the credit system works. Each round of fixes costs credits, so a loop of failed fixes is expensive on any plan. If a fix does not work after one or two tries, describe the problem more precisely, or restore an earlier version, instead of repeating the same request.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Lovable's docs suggest bookmarking milestones in version history and previewing the current version before a risky redesign, so you know which version to return to.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"When to pay for Lovable","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The free plan is enough to test an idea, build a simple landing page or a small internal tool and publish it on a lovable.app address. Pay for Pro when you need your own domain, want to edit or download the code, or keep running out of daily credits halfway through a project. Teams that need sign-in controls and shared workspaces are who Business is for.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Google just opened preorders for its Gemini glasses. They start at $395 and ship December 10
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Warby Parker's three frames start at $395. Gentle Monster's six frames start at $449. Samsung builds the hardware. Preorders opened on November 12. Stores and shipping start December 10, in the US and South Korea. Ask Gemini about what you are looking at, get Google Maps directions or live translation in over 70 languages. There is no screen. A 12MP camera and open-ear speakers do the work. A light shows when the camera records. If it is covered, recording stops. Sources: 9to5Google, Unite.AI, Android Headlines.

nf:hero.nf:alt: A pair of Warby Parker smart glasses made with Google, shown in a lifestyle product photo.

item.nf:article: {"headline":"Google opens preorders for Gemini smart glasses from Warby Parker and Gentle Monster, starting at $395","dek":"The display-free glasses, built by Samsung, have a camera, open-ear speakers and a Hey Gemini wake word, and reach stores on December 10.","summary":"Google opened preorders on November 12, 2026 for its first Gemini-powered Intelligent Eyewear, designed with Warby Parker and Gentle Monster and engineered by Samsung. Prices start at $395, and shipping and in-store sales begin December 10 in the US and South Korea.","seo_title":"Google Gemini glasses: price, release date and features","seo_description":"Google's Gemini smart glasses with Warby Parker and Gentle Monster start at $395 and ship December 10. Prices, features, privacy rules and compatible phones.","answer_summary":"Google's Gemini glasses start at $395 for Warby Parker frames and $449 for Gentle Monster frames. Preorders opened November 12, 2026, and they ship and reach stores on December 10.","tags":["Google","Gemini","Smart glasses","Samsung","Warby Parker","Gentle Monster"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Google opened preorders on November 12, 2026 for its Gemini-powered Intelligent Eyewear, a line of smart glasses designed with the eyewear brands Warby Parker and Gentle Monster and engineered by Samsung, according to 9to5Google and Unite.AI. Shipping and in-store availability begin on December 10.","sources":[{"name":"9to5Google","url":"https://9to5google.com/2026/11/12/google-intelligent-eyewear-glasses/"},{"name":"Unite.AI","url":"https://unite.ai/google-opens-pre-orders-for-gemini-powered-intelligent-eyewear"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Warby Parker's frames start at $395 and Gentle Monster's at $449, with Android Headlines putting the top Gentle Monster models at $489. Android Headlines counted 30 designs in total: 14 Warby Parker variations across three frames and 16 Gentle Monster variations across six frames.","sources":[{"name":"9to5Google","url":"https://9to5google.com/2026/11/12/google-intelligent-eyewear-glasses/"},{"name":"Android Headlines","url":"https://www.androidheadlines.com/2026/11/samsungs-smart-glasses-are-here-and-theyre-taking-privacy-more-seriously-than-meta.html"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"The frames and prices","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Warby Parker's three styles are called Alden, Reid and Wren, offered in optical and sun versions in Pine, Saddle and Jet Black, 9to5Google reported. Gentle Monster's six frames come in colors that include dark red, pink, gray and yellow, with clear, tinted, blue or brown lenses, and prescriptions are available for most designs. Unite.AI reported that more than 360 Warby Parker stores will offer guided demos, along with selected partner and Google Store locations.","sources":[{"name":"9to5Google","url":"https://9to5google.com/2026/11/12/google-intelligent-eyewear-glasses/"},{"name":"Unite.AI","url":"https://unite.ai/google-opens-pre-orders-for-gemini-powered-intelligent-eyewear"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The glasses have no display. They rely on a 12 megapixel ultra-wide camera that records video at up to 3K, four microphones and two open-ear speakers, running on a Qualcomm Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1 chip, according to 9to5Google. The frames weigh 40 to 44 grams, the battery is rated at nine hours, and the charging case holds seven full charges.","sources":[{"name":"9to5Google","url":"https://9to5google.com/2026/11/12/google-intelligent-eyewear-glasses/"},{"name":"Android Headlines","url":"https://www.androidheadlines.com/2026/11/samsungs-smart-glasses-are-here-and-theyre-taking-privacy-more-seriously-than-meta.html"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Gemini does on the glasses","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Wearers can wake the assistant with a new Hey Gemini phrase, a tap on the frame or, with a Pixel Watch, a hand gesture. Google lists questions about objects in view, turn-by-turn directions from Google Maps and real-time speech translation through Google Translate in more than 70 languages. The speakers also work as headphones for music, calls and spoken message summaries.","sources":[{"name":"9to5Google","url":"https://9to5google.com/2026/11/12/google-intelligent-eyewear-glasses/"},{"name":"Unite.AI","url":"https://unite.ai/google-opens-pre-orders-for-gemini-powered-intelligent-eyewear"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Unite.AI reported that Google's accessibility feature Guided Vision, which gives spoken descriptions of surroundings to blind and low-vision users, will also run on the glasses with a compatible Android phone. Google says the feature can make mistakes and is not a mobility aid.","sources":[{"name":"Unite.AI","url":"https://unite.ai/google-opens-pre-orders-for-gemini-powered-intelligent-eyewear"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Privacy rules","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"An outward-facing light turns on when the camera captures a photo or video, and recording stops if the light is covered or disabled, 9to5Google reported. Google says faces of bystanders are automatically redacted before Gemini processes what the camera sees, and that those camera visuals are not saved to Gemini History or used for AI training or ad targeting. A physical switch turns off the camera, microphones and Gemini.","sources":[{"name":"9to5Google","url":"https://9to5google.com/2026/11/12/google-intelligent-eyewear-glasses/"},{"name":"Unite.AI","url":"https://unite.ai/google-opens-pre-orders-for-gemini-powered-intelligent-eyewear"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Google Play rules bar apps on the glasses from using the camera for real-time facial identification, according to Unite.AI. Android Headlines reported that buyers must be 18 or older and pass age verification to activate the glasses.","sources":[{"name":"Unite.AI","url":"https://unite.ai/google-opens-pre-orders-for-gemini-powered-intelligent-eyewear"},{"name":"Android Headlines","url":"https://www.androidheadlines.com/2026/11/samsungs-smart-glasses-are-here-and-theyre-taking-privacy-more-seriously-than-meta.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The glasses work with Pixel 7 phones and newer, Galaxy S, Z Fold and Z Flip models on One UI 9.0 or later, and iPhone 13 Pro and newer, according to 9to5Google and Android Headlines.","sources":[{"name":"9to5Google","url":"https://9to5google.com/2026/11/12/google-intelligent-eyewear-glasses/"},{"name":"Android Headlines","url":"https://www.androidheadlines.com/2026/11/samsungs-smart-glasses-are-here-and-theyre-taking-privacy-more-seriously-than-meta.html"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The launch puts Google in direct competition with Meta's Ray-Ban glasses in the same form: a camera, speakers and an assistant inside frames that look like ordinary eyewear. Supporting iPhones from day one and leading with privacy controls suggests Google wants to reach buyers beyond its own phone users and answer the camera concerns that followed earlier smart glasses.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"The first reviews after the December 10 release should show whether the nine hour battery claim and the bystander face redaction hold up in daily use.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Google Flow to make AI videos, and what 50 free credits really buy
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Every account gets 50 Flow credits a day. Unused ones do not roll over. Free users may not get video between about 2 PM and 5 PM UTC. Omni Flash 1.2 costs 3 credits a second at 720p, so 10 seconds is 30 credits. Sources: Google Flow Help: Create videos in Flow, Google Flow Help: Flow models and supported features, Google Flow Help: Manage your Google Flow credits, Google Flow Help: Edit videos and build scenes, Google Flow Help: Get started with Flow, Google: New creative controls in Google Flow, Fello AI: Google Flow credits, prices and limits.
