item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use Google Flow: make AI videos step by step, and what 50 free credits get you","dek":"Google's AI filmmaking tool gives everyone 50 credits a day. Here is how to spend them, the steps to a first clip, and four prompts to copy.","summary":"Google Flow turns prompts, frames and reference images into short AI video clips, and every account gets 50 free credits a day. This guide covers credit costs, plans, the steps to a first video, frames, ingredients, the Flow Agent and Scenebuilder.","seo_title":"How to use Google Flow: AI video step by step (free credits)","seo_description":"How to use Google Flow: the 50 free daily credits, what each clip costs, steps to your first video, frames, ingredients, and four prompts to copy.","answer_summary":"Open Google Flow in Chrome or Edge, start a project, click the model name, choose Video, set the length and model, write a detailed prompt and click Generate. Everyone gets 50 credits a day; Omni Flash 1.2 costs 3 credits per second at 720p.","tags":["Google Flow","Gemini Omni","Veo","AI video","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"How to use Google Flow, in short: open it in Chrome or Edge, type a detailed prompt, pick a video model and length, and click Generate. Flow is Google's AI filmmaking tool for making clips, scenes and short stories with consistent characters, and every account gets 50 free credits a day.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: Get started with Flow","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16353333?hl=en"},{"name":"Google Flow Help: Manage your Google Flow credits","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16526234?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The catch: free credits buy only a few seconds of video at full quality, video generation can be unavailable to free users at peak hours, and the best editing features need a paid Google AI plan. This guide covers what you get for free, what each clip costs, the steps to a first video, and prompts to copy.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: Manage your Google Flow credits","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16526234?hl=en"},{"name":"Google Flow Help: Flow models and supported features","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16352836"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What you need to use Google Flow","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"You must be 18 or older, verify your age, and live in a supported region. Google says a VPN does not unlock Flow in an unsupported country, and Flow is not offered everywhere Google AI Pro is sold, so check the region list before you pay for a plan. Google recommends a computer for the strongest editing tools, and there is also a mobile app.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: Get started with Flow","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16353333?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Fello AI reported on November 10, 2026 that the Android app is in beta and the iPhone app is listed as coming soon. It also reports that Flow now lives at flow.google.com and that the old Google Labs address redirects there.","sources":[{"name":"Fello AI: Google Flow credits, prices and limits","url":"https://felloai.com/google-flow/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Google Flow free credits and plans","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Everyone gets 50 Flow credits per day, with or without a subscription. The daily credits refresh after your first generation of the day, and unused ones do not roll over. Without a subscription you may not be able to generate video between roughly 2 PM and 5 PM UTC, though images and the Flow Agent still work.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: Manage your Google Flow credits","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16526234?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Paid Google AI plans add monthly credits on top of the daily 50: 200 with Google AI Plus, 1,000 with Pro, 10,000 with the $100 Ultra plan and 25,000 with the $200 Ultra plan. Monthly credits reset at the start of the billing cycle and do not roll over either. Fello AI lists the US prices as $4.99 for Plus, $19.99 for Pro and $99.99 and $199.99 for the two Ultra tiers.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: Manage your Google Flow credits","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16526234?hl=en"},{"name":"Fello AI: Google Flow credits, prices and limits","url":"https://felloai.com/google-flow/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Credits are taken when a generation starts. If a generation fails or is blocked by a safety filter, Google says the credits come back within one hour.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: Get started with Flow","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16353333?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What a Google Flow video costs","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Omni Flash 1.2, the main video model, costs 1 credit per second at 360p and 3 credits per second at 720p for clips up to 10 seconds. So a 10 second 720p clip uses 30 of your 50 daily credits. Free users can make clips of 3 to 10 seconds; Plus, Pro and Ultra subscribers can go up to 15 seconds, at double the rate for seconds 11 to 15.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: Manage your Google Flow credits","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16526234?hl=en"},{"name":"Google Flow Help: Flow models and supported features","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16352836"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Veo 3.1 Lite makes 720p clips of 4, 6 or 8 seconds for 10 credits each, or 5 for Ultra subscribers. Veo 3.1 Fast, Veo 3.1 Quality and Omni Flash 1.1 will be retired on December 5, 2026, and Google recommends Omni Flash 1.2 or Veo 3.1 Lite for new projects. Image generation runs on Nano Banana models.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: Manage your Google Flow credits","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16526234?hl=en"},{"name":"Google Flow Help: Flow models and supported features","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16352836"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Draft at 360p, which costs a third of 720p, and only make the 720p version of the shot you like. Fello AI gives the same advice, and Google's own August update pitched 360p as the cheap way to test ideas.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to make your first video in Google Flow","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Open Flow and start a project","text":"Go to Google Flow in a Chromium browser such as Chrome or Edge, sign in, and open an existing project or start a new one.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Choose Video","text":"Click the model name in the prompt box (it starts on the image model Nano Banana Pro), then click Video.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Set the options","text":"Choose the aspect ratio, the number of outputs, the model and the length. Video is billed per second, so shorter clips cost less.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Write the prompt and generate","text":"Be specific about the subject, the action, the place, the lighting and the style, then click Generate.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: A first clip","text":"[Subject] [doing an action] in [place], [time of day] light, [style, for example handheld documentary or warm film look]. The camera [moves slowly toward the subject / stays still].","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Frames, ingredients and the Flow Agent","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Frames to video lets you set a start frame, an end frame or both. Click the model name, then Video, then Frames, drag in your images, and describe the action between them. This mode works only on the web version of Flow.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: Create videos in Flow","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16353334?hl=en"},{"name":"Google Flow Help: Flow models and supported features","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16352836"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Connect a start and end frame","text":"The camera moves from the first image to the second in one smooth shot. [Describe what happens in between, for example: the door opens and the dog runs out into the snow.]","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Ingredients are reference images or videos for a character, a product or a place. Click the model name, then Video, then Ingredients, and add references by dragging them in, typing @ to search your project, or clicking Add. Then say how each one should appear. Google suggests plain backgrounds for subject and product references and a prompt that matches the references.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: Create videos in Flow","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16353334?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Use your ingredients","text":"The [character from @ingredient] walks into [place] holding [product from @ingredient]. Keep the face and clothes exactly as in the reference. [Lighting and mood].","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The Flow Agent is a switch in the prompt box. Turn on Agent, describe the scene, and you can ask for several versions at once; Google's own example is a request for 5 variations of a video with different lighting. You can also drag a finished clip into the prompt box with Agent on and describe a change, and the edit is saved to that clip's stack.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: Create videos in Flow","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16353334?hl=en"},{"name":"Google Flow Help: Edit videos and build scenes","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16935718?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Ask the Agent for options","text":"Give me 4 variations of this video with different lighting: early morning, noon, sunset and night. Keep the subject and camera move the same.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Extend clips and build a scene","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Extending a clip needs a Google AI Plus, Pro or Ultra plan and Omni Flash 1.2. Click the clip, click Extend, pick the extra length, describe how the action continues and click Generate. You can add up to 3 reference images. Veo Extend was retired on November 5, 2026.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: Edit videos and build scenes","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16935718?hl=en"},{"name":"Google Flow Help: Manage your Google Flow credits","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16526234?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Scenebuilder puts several clips in order. Hover over a clip, click More, then Add to Scene. From there you can drag clips into order, trim the start and end of each one, preview the sequence and download the scene. To keep a single frame, pause the video, hover over it and click Save frame, then use it as an ingredient or a start or end frame.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: Edit videos and build scenes","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16935718?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Subscribers can upscale Omni 360p videos to 1080p, and Ultra subscribers to 4K. Every Flow output carries an invisible SynthID watermark, and a visible watermark can be switched on in the profile menu.","sources":[{"name":"Google Flow Help: Flow models and supported features","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16352836"},{"name":"Google Flow Help: Get started with Flow","url":"https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16353333?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where Google Flow falls short","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The free plan is fine for learning the tool, not for a project. Fifty credits are less than two 10 second clips at 720p, they reset daily rather than piling up, and the peak hour block lands in the US morning. Region limits are strict, and features such as frames to video and extending are web only or paid only. If you want to test Flow seriously, Google AI Plus is the cheapest way to get longer clips, extending and free 1080p upscaling.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Before a bigger project, check your balance: click your profile picture at the top right in Flow. Google notes that limits and credit costs can change, and the current cost shows in the prompt box settings.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Anthropic is saving up to 20% of its IPO for regular investors, at $70 to $78 a share
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Anthropic plans to sell 825 million shares at an expected $70 to $78 each. At the top of the range that is up to $64.35 billion. An updated filing on November 10 says up to 20% could go to retail investors. Fidelity, Robinhood, Charles Schwab, SoFi and ETRADE are taking requests from eligible customers, CoinCentral reports. A request is not a guarantee. If demand is higher than supply, many will get fewer shares or none. Sources: Yahoo Finance, CoinCentral, Anthropic on X, MarsBit via KuCoin.

nf:hero.nf:alt: Portrait photo of a smiling man.

item.nf:article: {"headline":"Anthropic reserves up to 20% of its IPO for retail investors","dek":"The Claude maker expects to price its shares at $70 to $78, with trading on Nasdaq possible as early as November 19.","summary":"Anthropic said in an updated filing that up to 20% of its initial public offering could go to retail investors. The company plans to sell 825 million shares at an expected $70 to $78 each.","seo_title":"Anthropic IPO: up to 20% for retail investors, $70 to $78","seo_description":"Anthropic may give retail investors up to 20% of its IPO at $70 to $78 a share. Brokers, key dates and what happened after SpaceX did the same.","answer_summary":"Anthropic says up to 20% of its IPO shares could be allocated to retail investors, at an expected price of $70 to $78 a share. Trading under the ticker ANT could begin on Nasdaq as early as November 19, 2026.","tags":["Anthropic","IPO","Claude","Nasdaq","Retail investors"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI models, said in an updated regulatory filing on November 10, 2026, that up to 20% of the shares in its initial public offering could be allocated to retail investors, according to Yahoo Finance. The company plans to offer 825 million shares of Class A common stock at an expected price of $70 to $78 per share. At the top of that range the offering would be worth up to $64.35 billion.","sources":[{"name":"Yahoo Finance","url":"https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/anthropic-reserving-20-ipo-retail-213904527.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Anthropic also shared a link to a dedicated IPO website, ipo.anthropic.com, in a post on X, along with a notice that it has filed a registration statement and prospectus with the Securities and Exchange Commission and that investors should read the prospectus before investing.","sources":[{"name":"Anthropic on X","url":"https://x.com/AnthropicAI/status/2120841731302154708"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How retail investors can request shares","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Eligible customers of Fidelity, Robinhood, Charles Schwab, SoFi and ETRADE can request shares through those brokers, CoinCentral reported on November 12, 2026. Fidelity customers must submit an indication of interest before an expected deadline of November 17. A request does not guarantee an allocation if demand is higher than the number of shares available, and access varies by country, the outlet said.","sources":[{"name":"CoinCentral","url":"https://coincentral.com/how-to-invest-in-the-anthropic-ipo-share-price-date-and-risks-explained"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Outside the United States, a report by MarsBit republished by KuCoin said the IPO website has regional paths for the US, the UK, Canada, Australia and Japan, and named Interactive Brokers, Revolut and SBI as participating institutions. That report cites unnamed filings and has not been confirmed by Anthropic.","sources":[{"name":"MarsBit via KuCoin","url":"https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/anthropic-ipo-website-launched-retail-investors-in-multiple-countries-can-apply"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Key dates and numbers","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Pricing is expected on November 18, and trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT could begin as early as November 19, according to CoinCentral, which noted that the dates can change and that the opening price could land above or below the expected range. Yahoo Finance estimated the retail portion at about $12.2 billion at the $74 midpoint.","sources":[{"name":"Yahoo Finance","url":"https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/anthropic-reserving-20-ipo-retail-213904527.html"},{"name":"CoinCentral","url":"https://coincentral.com/how-to-invest-in-the-anthropic-ipo-share-price-date-and-risks-explained"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The filing shows third quarter revenue of $17 billion, more than 12 times the figure a year earlier, and more than 11,900 customers that spend at least $100,000 a year, Yahoo Finance reported. It also lists about $900.9 billion in committed spending, most of it for computing infrastructure, with about $451.6 billion expected before the end of 2030.","sources":[{"name":"Yahoo Finance","url":"https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/anthropic-reserving-20-ipo-retail-213904527.html"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What happened in earlier offerings","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Retail investors received about 20% of SpaceX's offering as well, Yahoo Finance said, citing The Wall Street Journal. That stock priced at $135, opened at $150 and passed $200 by its third day, and was later trading below $150. Facebook opened at $38 on May 17, 2012, and was under $18 by early September of that year.","sources":[{"name":"Yahoo Finance","url":"https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/anthropic-reserving-20-ipo-retail-213904527.html"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"In NeuraFeed's reading, a large retail allocation does two things at once. It lets the people who use Claude every day own a piece of the company on the same terms as institutions, and it moves part of the first-day price risk onto buyers who have the least information. The SpaceX and Facebook examples show that a strong opening and a lower price a few weeks later can both happen to the same stock. The size of Anthropic's spending commitments, more than fifty times its latest quarterly revenue, is the number in the filing that deserves the most attention from anyone weighing a request.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"Watch the final price set on November 18 and how many shares retail investors actually receive, since both will show how much demand exists outside the large funds before trading begins.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Russian pranksters fooled OpenAI's national security team with a fake Ukrainian official on a 17-minute call
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Russian prank duo Vovan and Lexus posed as Rustem Umerov, a top Ukrainian security official, on a 17-minute video call with OpenAI. The fake Umerov kept his camera off. The duo later posted the recording online. Three senior OpenAI staff joined, including Sasha Baker, its head of national security policy. They discussed helping Ukraine's military, even offensive uses. One of them said many senior people at OpenAI were reluctant about offensive uses. Sources: The Intercept, Business Today, Digit.

nf:hero.nf:alt: A speaker on stage at a Semafor conference in New York.

item.nf:article: {"headline":"Russian pranksters posed as a Ukrainian official on a call with OpenAI security staff","dek":"Three OpenAI national security officials spent 17 minutes discussing military AI with an impostor before the company concluded it was a prank.","summary":"Russian comedy duo Vovan and Lexus impersonated Ukrainian security official Rustem Umerov on a 17-minute video call with three OpenAI national security officials, The Intercept reported on November 11, 2026. OpenAI said it investigated, concluded the call was a prank and changed its procedures.","seo_title":"Russian pranksters fooled OpenAI national security officials","seo_description":"Vovan and Lexus posed as Ukraine's Rustem Umerov on a 17-minute video call with three OpenAI officials about military AI. OpenAI calls it a prank.","answer_summary":"Three OpenAI national security officials held a 17-minute video call with Russian pranksters posing as Ukrainian official Rustem Umerov. OpenAI says it investigated, concluded it was a prank and took steps to prevent a repeat.","tags":["OpenAI","Ukraine","Vovan and Lexus","AI security","Military AI"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Three senior OpenAI national security officials spent 17 minutes on a video call with a man they believed was Rustem Umerov, a senior Ukrainian security official, according to a report The Intercept published on November 11, 2026. The caller was in fact part of Vovan and Lexus, a Russian comedy duo known for prank calls, and the pair later posted a recording of the conversation online.","sources":[{"name":"The Intercept","url":"https://theintercept.com/2026/11/11/openai-ukraine-russia-prank-security/"},{"name":"Business Today","url":"https://www.businesstoday.in/technology/news/story/russian-pranksters-fooled-3-senior-openai-officials-got-them-talking-about-ukraines-military-ai-needs-567102-2026-11-12"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenAI spokesperson Nate Evans told The Intercept that the company had opened an investigation into the call's authenticity weeks earlier, worked internally and with the relevant authorities, and concluded that it was a prank. He said OpenAI had taken action to prevent similar situations in the future. The company did not say when the call took place or which measures it adopted, according to Digit.","sources":[{"name":"The Intercept","url":"https://theintercept.com/2026/11/11/openai-ukraine-russia-prank-security/"},{"name":"Digit","url":"https://www.digit.in/news/general/openai-security-officials-reportedly-fooled-by-russian-pranksters-in-shocking-17-minute-call-here-is-what-happened.html"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Who was on the call","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The OpenAI participants were Sasha Baker, who leads national security policy at the company and previously held a senior Defense Department post; Caroline Zier, OpenAI's lead for strategic initiatives, who also worked at the Defense Department; and Ben Crampton, who leads the company's European national security work and previously worked for the European Union and the United Nations, The Intercept reported.","sources":[{"name":"The Intercept","url":"https://theintercept.com/2026/11/11/openai-ukraine-russia-prank-security/"},{"name":"Business Today","url":"https://www.businesstoday.in/technology/news/story/russian-pranksters-fooled-3-senior-openai-officials-got-them-talking-about-ukraines-military-ai-needs-567102-2026-11-12"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Baker and Zier said during the call that they had met Umerov before. The impersonator appears to have kept his camera off. Vladimir Kuznetsov, one of the two pranksters, told The Intercept that the duo first reached a senior Ukrainian official in San Francisco while posing as Umerov, and that this official believed he was setting up a meeting with OpenAI.","sources":[{"name":"The Intercept","url":"https://theintercept.com/2026/11/11/openai-ukraine-russia-prank-security/"},{"name":"Digit","url":"https://www.digit.in/news/general/openai-security-officials-reportedly-fooled-by-russian-pranksters-in-shocking-17-minute-call-here-is-what-happened.html"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What the officials discussed","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The fake official asked about OpenAI's possible military support for Ukraine, including offensive capabilities. Crampton said the company wanted as deep a relationship with Ukraine as possible but might not reach that goal right away. He also described a general reluctance among many senior people at OpenAI about offensive military uses, and said offense and defense cannot always be told apart, according to accounts of the recording.","sources":[{"name":"The Intercept","url":"https://theintercept.com/2026/11/11/openai-ukraine-russia-prank-security/"},{"name":"Business Today","url":"https://www.businesstoday.in/technology/news/story/russian-pranksters-fooled-3-senior-openai-officials-got-them-talking-about-ukraines-military-ai-needs-567102-2026-11-12"},{"name":"Digit","url":"https://www.digit.in/news/general/openai-security-officials-reportedly-fooled-by-russian-pranksters-in-shocking-17-minute-call-here-is-what-happened.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The officials mentioned Daybreak Blue, an OpenAI model that finds and fixes computer vulnerabilities, and a developing partnership with Ukraine's Ministry of Defense. Baker said OpenAI had been in contact with the Pentagon about helping Ukraine. When the caller asked whether OpenAI could help counter Elon Musk's influence, Baker said the company probably could not help with Musk.","sources":[{"name":"The Intercept","url":"https://theintercept.com/2026/11/11/openai-ukraine-russia-prank-security/"},{"name":"Business Today","url":"https://www.businesstoday.in/technology/news/story/russian-pranksters-fooled-3-senior-openai-officials-got-them-talking-about-ukraines-military-ai-needs-567102-2026-11-12"},{"name":"Digit","url":"https://www.digit.in/news/general/openai-security-officials-reportedly-fooled-by-russian-pranksters-in-shocking-17-minute-call-here-is-what-happened.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Business Today, citing The Intercept, noted that OpenAI has an ongoing $200 million contract with the U.S. Department of War to supply AI applications for military users.","sources":[{"name":"Business Today","url":"https://www.businesstoday.in/technology/news/story/russian-pranksters-fooled-3-senior-openai-officials-got-them-talking-about-ukraines-military-ai-needs-567102-2026-11-12"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Who Vovan and Lexus are","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Vovan and Lexus are the pseudonyms of Vladimir Kuznetsov and Alexei Stolyarov, according to Digit. They have made prank calls to public figures since 2011, including Elton John and the late Senator John McCain. Their pranks often line up with Russian foreign policy, and they have been accused of working with the Russian government, which they deny. The Ukrainian Embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to The Intercept's request for comment.","sources":[{"name":"The Intercept","url":"https://theintercept.com/2026/11/11/openai-ukraine-russia-prank-security/"},{"name":"Business Today","url":"https://www.businesstoday.in/technology/news/story/russian-pranksters-fooled-3-senior-openai-officials-got-them-talking-about-ukraines-military-ai-needs-567102-2026-11-12"},{"name":"Digit","url":"https://www.digit.in/news/general/openai-security-officials-reportedly-fooled-by-russian-pranksters-in-shocking-17-minute-call-here-is-what-happened.html"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The episode shows how much weight a familiar name and title can carry in a remote meeting. The call reached OpenAI through a real Ukrainian official, and two of the three participants believed they already knew the person on the other end. For an AI company that now works with defense customers, conversations about military uses carry far higher stakes than an ordinary sales call, and a caller with the camera off is a gap that formal identity checks can close without relying on recognition.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"The next signal to watch is whether OpenAI or other AI labs describe the identity checks they now require before national security conversations, and whether Ukrainian officials explain how the introduction to OpenAI was arranged.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: AI just gave Geralt's voice actor his old voice back
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Jacek Rozenek, the Polish voice of Geralt, had a stroke in 2019 that left him unable to speak. He came back to voice acting in 2022 after hours of training a day. His voice had changed. For the new expansion, Songs of the Past, Rozenek recorded every line himself. CD Projekt Red gave AI voice firm Respeecher all his old Witcher 3 lines to build a model, which made the new lines sound like him 12 years ago. Rozenek agreed to it. CD Projekt Red says its contracts require consent for any AI work and calls this a special case. Sources: Video Games Chronicle, GamesRadar+, Nintendo Life.

nf:hero.nf:alt: Geralt of Rivia, the white haired hero of The Witcher 3, in a scene from the game.

item.nf:article: {"headline":"CD Projekt Red used AI to restore Geralt's Polish voice after the actor's stroke","dek":"Jacek Rozenek recorded new lines for The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past himself, and a Respeecher model trained on his original performance brought them closer to how he sounded in the original game.","summary":"CD Projekt Red worked with the AI voice company Respeecher to adjust the Polish voice of Geralt in the upcoming Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past, after actor Jacek Rozenek's voice changed following a 2019 stroke. Rozenek consented, and the studio says it uses AI on performances only with consent.","seo_title":"Witcher 3 Songs of the Past: AI used on Geralt's Polish voice","seo_description":"CD Projekt Red and Respeecher used AI, with actor Jacek Rozenek's consent, to make his new Geralt lines match his voice from before his 2019 stroke.","answer_summary":"Yes. CD Projekt Red used an AI model from Respeecher, trained on Jacek Rozenek's original Witcher 3 recordings, to adjust the new Polish Geralt lines he recorded for Songs of the Past. Rozenek agreed to it, and the English version with Doug Cockle needed no AI changes.","tags":["CD Projekt Red","The Witcher 3","Respeecher","AI voice","Video games"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"CD Projekt Red used artificial intelligence to adjust the Polish voice of Geralt of Rivia in Songs of the Past, the upcoming expansion for The Witcher 3, according to reports published on November 11, 2026, by Video Games Chronicle and GamesRadar+. The voice actor, Jacek Rozenek, suffered a stroke in 2019, and his voice changed as he recovered.","sources":[{"name":"Video Games Chronicle","url":"https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/the-witcher-3-expansion-uses-ai-to-adjust-geralts-polish-voiceover-because-the-actor-suffered-a-stroke/"},{"name":"GamesRadar+","url":"https://www.gamesradar.com/games/the-witcher/cd-projekt-red-worked-with-an-ai-company-on-geralts-polish-voice-in-the-witcher-3-songs-of-the-past-with-the-original-actors-approval-after-health-concerns/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Rozenek is the longtime Polish voice of Geralt. Video Games Chronicle reported that the stroke left Rozenek unable to speak and that he returned to voice acting in 2022 after training for hours a day.","sources":[{"name":"Video Games Chronicle","url":"https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/the-witcher-3-expansion-uses-ai-to-adjust-geralts-polish-voiceover-because-the-actor-suffered-a-stroke/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How the AI was used","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Rozenek recorded the new lines for the expansion himself, in the usual way. The studio then sent the lines he had recorded for the base game of The Witcher 3 to Respeecher, a Ukrainian company that builds AI voice models. Respeecher trained a model on that original performance and used it to retouch the new recordings so they sit closer to the voice players heard in the base game.","sources":[{"name":"Video Games Chronicle","url":"https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/the-witcher-3-expansion-uses-ai-to-adjust-geralts-polish-voiceover-because-the-actor-suffered-a-stroke/"},{"name":"GamesRadar+","url":"https://www.gamesradar.com/games/the-witcher/cd-projekt-red-worked-with-an-ai-company-on-geralts-polish-voice-in-the-witcher-3-songs-of-the-past-with-the-original-actors-approval-after-health-concerns/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to GamesRadar+, the new lines clashed with the original dialogue without that step. Mikołaj Szwed, a localization producer at CD Projekt Red, said in the interview that the studio delivered to Respeecher all of the lines Rozenek had recorded for The Witcher 3. Respeecher's Dmytry Vasylets described the brief as making the actor's voice sound alive, rich and young, as it did in the original game.","sources":[{"name":"GamesRadar+","url":"https://www.gamesradar.com/games/the-witcher/cd-projekt-red-worked-with-an-ai-company-on-geralts-polish-voice-in-the-witcher-3-songs-of-the-past-with-the-original-actors-approval-after-health-concerns/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Rozenek said the goal was for the voice to be as close as possible to his voice from 12 years earlier, and he said he has great trust in the people who make the game. Both outlets reported that he consented to the use of AI on his performance. The interview was first published by Game File.","sources":[{"name":"Video Games Chronicle","url":"https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/the-witcher-3-expansion-uses-ai-to-adjust-geralts-polish-voiceover-because-the-actor-suffered-a-stroke/"},{"name":"GamesRadar+","url":"https://www.gamesradar.com/games/the-witcher/cd-projekt-red-worked-with-an-ai-company-on-geralts-polish-voice-in-the-witcher-3-songs-of-the-past-with-the-original-actors-approval-after-health-concerns/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"A case the studio calls special","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"CD Projekt Red says its contracts require consent for any AI work on a performance, and that it turned to AI here only because of Rozenek's health situation. Szwed called it a special case and said he sees it as a way to use AI ethically, with consent, to do something good. The studio has worked with Respeecher before, on a Cyberpunk 2077 character whose actor had died, GamesRadar+ reported.","sources":[{"name":"GamesRadar+","url":"https://www.gamesradar.com/games/the-witcher/cd-projekt-red-worked-with-an-ai-company-on-geralts-polish-voice-in-the-witcher-3-songs-of-the-past-with-the-original-actors-approval-after-health-concerns/"},{"name":"Video Games Chronicle","url":"https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/the-witcher-3-expansion-uses-ai-to-adjust-geralts-polish-voiceover-because-the-actor-suffered-a-stroke/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The English version of Geralt, voiced by Doug Cockle, did not need any AI retouching for the expansion, according to GamesRadar+. Nintendo Life reported that Songs of the Past is due next year, in 2027.","sources":[{"name":"GamesRadar+","url":"https://www.gamesradar.com/games/the-witcher/cd-projekt-red-worked-with-an-ai-company-on-geralts-polish-voice-in-the-witcher-3-songs-of-the-past-with-the-original-actors-approval-after-health-concerns/"},{"name":"Nintendo Life","url":"https://www.nintendolife.com/news/2026/11/witcher-3s-new-expansion-pairs-geralts-polish-voice-actor-with-ai-but-its-a-special-case"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Most arguments about AI voices in games turn on copying a performer without permission. This case is built differently: the actor still performs every line, the model is trained only on his own earlier work for the same character, and he signed off on it. That combination of consent, the same performer and a narrow purpose is likely to be cited as a reference point in future arguments over where AI voice tools belong in game production.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"The next test is how players react when Songs of the Past ships in 2027, and whether other studios adopt the same consent based approach for veteran actors whose voices have changed with age or illness.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: United Airlines just banned AI assistants from booking your flights, even through travel agencies
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: United says it will stop unauthorized, third-party AI agents from booking flights for travelers, on its site and app and through travel agencies. AI tools can still show United's flights and fares. They just cannot finish the purchase. United says giving your login to an AI assistant can expose sensitive information, and the bot could buy tickets, change your account or spend MileagePlus miles. Check-in is an issue too: federal rules make travelers confirm their bags hold no banned items. Sources: CBS News, Air Data News.

nf:hero.nf:alt: A United Airlines Boeing 737 MAX passenger jet.

item.nf:article: {"headline":"United Airlines bans unauthorized AI agents from booking flights for travelers","dek":"The airline says personal AI assistants could expose account data, make unwanted purchases or spend MileagePlus miles, and it will block them on its own channels and through travel agencies.","summary":"United Airlines said on November 11, 2026, that it will prohibit unauthorized third-party AI agents from booking flights on travelers' behalf. The restriction covers United's website and app as well as travel agencies and aggregators, while AI tools may still display United's flights and fares.","seo_title":"United Airlines bans AI agents from booking flights","seo_description":"United will block unauthorized AI agents from booking its flights on its site, its app and through travel agencies, citing security and federal rules.","answer_summary":"Unauthorized AI agents such as personal AI assistants can no longer complete United Airlines bookings for travelers, either on United's own platforms or through travel agencies. They can still show United flights and fares.","tags":["United Airlines","AI agents","Travel","Meta","OpenAI"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"United Airlines said on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, that it will ban unauthorized third-party AI agents and assistants from making flight reservations on behalf of travelers, according to CBS News. The airline is updating its booking, ticketing and distribution policies to put the rule into effect, Air Data News reported.","sources":[{"name":"CBS News","url":"https://www.cbsnews.com/news/united-airlines-bans-ai-agents-booking-flights/"},{"name":"Air Data News","url":"https://www.airdatanews.com/united-airlines-blocks-ai-agents-from-booking-flights-citing-security-risks/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The restriction applies to United's own digital platforms and also to indirect channels, meaning travel agencies and ticket aggregators. According to Air Data News, the policy does not stop AI assistants from showing United's flights and fares; it stops them from completing reservations through the airline's systems without authorization. United did not announce a specific timetable for enforcement.","sources":[{"name":"CBS News","url":"https://www.cbsnews.com/news/united-airlines-bans-ai-agents-booking-flights/"},{"name":"Air Data News","url":"https://www.airdatanews.com/united-airlines-blocks-ai-agents-from-booking-flights-citing-security-risks/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"CBS News cited Meta's Muse and OpenAI's dots as examples of the consumer AI agents that have started to book travel and handle other tasks for their users.","sources":[{"name":"CBS News","url":"https://www.cbsnews.com/news/united-airlines-bans-ai-agents-booking-flights/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"The reasons United gave","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"United's main argument is security. The airline said that sharing account credentials with personal third-party AI assistants can expose sensitive information, and that actions taken by these tools can lead to purchases, account changes or use of MileagePlus miles that the customer did not intend, according to CBS News and Air Data News.","sources":[{"name":"CBS News","url":"https://www.cbsnews.com/news/united-airlines-bans-ai-agents-booking-flights/"},{"name":"Air Data News","url":"https://www.airdatanews.com/united-airlines-blocks-ai-agents-from-booking-flights-citing-security-risks/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The airline also pointed to federal rules. At check-in, passengers must confirm that their luggage contains no prohibited items, and United said letting an agent handle that step without the traveler's direct confirmation could conflict with those requirements. Air Data News reported that United plans to update its Digital Trust Center to explain the change and to help customers affected by unintended actions taken by AI assistants.","sources":[{"name":"CBS News","url":"https://www.cbsnews.com/news/united-airlines-bans-ai-agents-booking-flights/"},{"name":"Air Data News","url":"https://www.airdatanews.com/united-airlines-blocks-ai-agents-from-booking-flights-citing-security-risks/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Reservations completed by such tools before November 11 will be honored, according to Travel Weekly as cited by Air Data News. The airline said it will keep evaluating how third-party AI tools interact with its services, which leaves room for authorizing specific platforms later.","sources":[{"name":"Air Data News","url":"https://www.airdatanews.com/united-airlines-blocks-ai-agents-from-booking-flights-citing-security-risks/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Control of the customer relationship","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"United chief executive Scott Kirby said at an event in Chicago on November 10 that he did not want to create another intermediary between the airline and its customers, The Wall Street Journal reported, as cited by Air Data News. Henry Harteveldt of Atmosphere Research Group told CBS News that the policy suggests United wants to keep control of the booking process, and that it likely also wants to avoid the costs of a surge in flight searches run by AI bots.","sources":[{"name":"CBS News","url":"https://www.cbsnews.com/news/united-airlines-bans-ai-agents-booking-flights/"},{"name":"Air Data News","url":"https://www.airdatanews.com/united-airlines-blocks-ai-agents-from-booking-flights-citing-security-risks/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Other carriers are taking a different approach. Delta Air Lines has indicated that properly authenticated AI assistants can make reservations, with additional safeguards for sensitive transactions, according to Air Data News. Southwest Airlines has made its flight inventory available to ChatGPT users. Harteveldt told CBS News that United fares can still be booked through Kayak, Hopper and Google Flights.","sources":[{"name":"CBS News","url":"https://www.cbsnews.com/news/united-airlines-bans-ai-agents-booking-flights/"},{"name":"Air Data News","url":"https://www.airdatanews.com/united-airlines-blocks-ai-agents-from-booking-flights-citing-security-risks/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The decision draws a clear line between AI tools that help travelers search and AI tools that act inside a customer's account. United is leaving the first kind alone and closing the door on the second unless it has approved the platform, which keeps the airline in charge of the final sale and of the data that comes with it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"The next signal is whether United authorizes any specific AI platform to book on its systems, and whether other large carriers follow its approach or Delta's.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Runway AI to make videos, and what the free plan really gets you
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Free accounts get 125 credits once. They never expire but never refresh. Gen-4.5 video needs the Standard plan or higher. Gen-4.5 costs 12 credits a second, so 5 seconds is 60 credits. Gen-4 Turbo costs 5 a second. Runway suggests testing there first. Camera shot, subject, action, place, then light and style. Sources: Runway Help Center: How do credits work, Runway Help Center: Gen-4.5, Runway Help Center: Text to Video prompting guide, Runway Help Center: Creating with Gen-4, Runway Help Center: Standard plan, Runway: Introducing Runway Gen-4.5, eesel AI: Runway AI pricing in 2026.
item.category: Runway Help Center: How do credits work
Runway Help Center: Text to Video prompting guide
Runway Help Center: Creating with Gen-4

nf:hero.nf:alt: Runway's announcement card for its Gen-4.5 video model.

item.nf:article:
{"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use Runway AI video generator: a beginner guide","dek":"What the free plan really includes, what each second of video costs, and three prompt patterns from Runway's own guides.","summary":"Runway's Gen-4.5 video model needs a paid plan and costs 12 credits per second of video. This guide covers the free plan, credit costs, the steps to a first clip, and prompts to copy.","seo_title":"How to use Runway AI video generator: a beginner guide","seo_description":"How to use Runway AI step by step: what the free plan includes, credits per second, making a Gen-4.5 video, and three prompts to copy.","answer_summary":"Open Runway on the web, choose Gen-4.5 in Video mode, type a prompt or drop in an image, pick 5, 8 or 10 seconds and click Generate. Gen-4.5 needs the Standard plan or higher and costs 12 credits per second.","tags":["Runway","AI video","Gen-4.5","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"How to use Runway AI comes down to three things: knowing which plan unlocks the video models, writing prompts in the order Runway's own guide recommends, and watching the credit cost of every clip. Runway is a web app for AI video, images and audio, and its newest video model, Gen-4.5, makes clips from a text prompt or from a still image.","sources":[{"name":"Runway Help Center: Gen-4.5","url":"https://help.runwayml.com/hc/en-us/articles/46974685288467"},{"name":"Runway Help Center: How do credits work","url":"https://help.runwayml.com/hc/en-us/articles/15124877443219-How-do-credits-work"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The short version: the free plan gives you 125 credits once and does not include Gen-4.5, which needs the Standard plan or higher. Gen-4.5 costs 12 credits per second of video and outputs 720p clips at 24 frames per second.","sources":[{"name":"Runway Help Center: How do credits work","url":"https://help.runwayml.com/hc/en-us/articles/15124877443219-How-do-credits-work"},{"name":"Runway Help Center: Gen-4.5","url":"https://help.runwayml.com/hc/en-us/articles/46974685288467"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What the Runway free plan gets you","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Free accounts get a one-time deposit of 125 credits. Those credits do not expire, but they also do not refresh, and free users cannot buy more, according to Runway's help center. Paid plans come with monthly credits: 625 on Standard, 2,250 on Pro and on Unlimited, and 9,500 on Max.","sources":[{"name":"Runway Help Center: How do credits work","url":"https://help.runwayml.com/hc/en-us/articles/15124877443219-How-do-credits-work"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"A pricing review from eesel AI, last updated August 31, 2026, says the free plan covers text to image, text to speech and the image and audio apps, while the Gen-4 and Gen-4.5 video models need Standard or higher. It lists Standard at $12 per user per month billed yearly, about $15 month to month, and Pro at $28 per user per month billed yearly, about $35 month to month.","sources":[{"name":"eesel AI: Runway AI pricing in 2026","url":"https://www.eesel.ai/en/blog/runway-ai-pricing"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Monthly credits on Standard, Pro and Unlimited do not roll over: they reset within 24 hours of your billing date. Max can carry up to one month of unused credits forward. Credits you buy on top of a paid plan do not expire, and the minimum purchase is 1,000 credits.","sources":[{"name":"Runway Help Center: How do credits work","url":"https://help.runwayml.com/hc/en-us/articles/15124877443219-How-do-credits-work"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"In practice, the free account is a way to test Runway's image and audio tools, not its headline video model. If video is the reason you came, plan on Standard at minimum.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How much a Runway AI video costs","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Runway's credits page lists Gen-4.5 at 12 credits per second, so a 5 second clip costs 60 credits and a 10 second clip costs 120. Gen-4 also costs 12 credits per second, while Gen-4 Turbo costs 5 credits per second, or 25 credits for 5 seconds. Runway's Gen-4 guide suggests testing an idea in Turbo first and switching to the full model only if the result falls short.","sources":[{"name":"Runway Help Center: How do credits work","url":"https://help.runwayml.com/hc/en-us/articles/15124877443219-How-do-credits-work"},{"name":"Runway Help Center: Creating with Gen-4","url":"https://help.runwayml.com/hc/en-us/articles/37327109429011-Creating-with-Gen-4"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Runway's guide to the Standard plan gives its own ways to stretch credits: start with 5 second videos instead of 10, experiment with image models before moving to video, and start video generations without audio. It notes that third-party models and video with audio use credits faster, while image models and Turbo video models use fewer.","sources":[{"name":"Runway Help Center: Standard plan","url":"https://help.runwayml.com/hc/en-us/articles/49191105352339"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Runway's own pages do not always show the same total for every length, so check the cost shown in the app before you press Generate, not after.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to make your first Runway AI video with Gen-4.5","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Pick the model","text":"Open Runway on the web, go to Video creation mode and choose Gen-4.5 in the model selector at the bottom left. Gen-4.5 is web only, so do this in a browser, not the phone app.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Choose text or an image","text":"For Text to Video, type a prompt only. For Image to Video, drag a picture into the prompt window first, then write the prompt. The image becomes the look of the shot, so the text only has to describe what moves.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Set length and shape","text":"Pick 5, 8 or 10 seconds. Runway says prompts with several actions in a row work better with longer clips. Then choose an aspect ratio: 16:9 for YouTube, 9:16 for Reels and TikTok, 1:1 for a square post. Runway also offers 4:3, 3:4 and 21:9.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Generate and keep the good one","text":"Click Generate and wait. Under the right side of the result you can favorite, upscale or download it. The Use button on the left sends the clip on to the next tool so you can keep working on it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Change one thing at a time","text":"If the clip is close but wrong, edit the prompt and run it again. Change one element per run so you can tell what fixed it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Runway prompts that work (copy and paste)","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Runway's Text to Video guide says every prompt needs two parts: what is in the frame and how it moves. It recommends full sentences over a list of keywords for control, and suggests this order: the camera shot, the subject, the action, the environment, then supporting details such as light and style. Its own example is a medium shot of a cowboy on a horse in a dusty setting.","sources":[{"name":"Runway Help Center: Text to Video prompting guide","url":"https://help.runwayml.com/hc/en-us/articles/42460036199443"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Text to Video, the basic structure","text":"[Camera] shot of [subject] [doing what] in [place]. [Light, weather or mood]. [How the camera moves].

Example: Medium shot of a barista pouring milk into a cup in a small cafe. Soft morning light from the window. The camera slowly pushes in.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Image to Video, motion only","text":"The woman turns her head toward the camera and smiles. Her hair moves in the wind. The camera stays still.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"For Image to Video, Runway's Gen-4 guide says the picture already sets the subject, colors, lighting and style, so the prompt should be almost entirely about motion. Text prompts there can be up to 1,000 characters.","sources":[{"name":"Runway Help Center: Creating with Gen-4","url":"https://help.runwayml.com/hc/en-us/articles/37327109429011-Creating-with-Gen-4"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Timing with timestamps","text":"Close-up of a man at a desk in a dark office.
[00:00 through 00:02] he looks away, then turns toward the camera
[00:02 through 00:03] fast zoom in to frame his eyes","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Runway calls this timestamp prompting and recommends pairing the timed lines with a normal sentence. Give each action a realistic length: the guide points out that walking across a room takes about three seconds, not half a second.","sources":[{"name":"Runway Help Center: Text to Video prompting guide","url":"https://help.runwayml.com/hc/en-us/articles/42460036199443"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If something you asked for does not show up, say it again more plainly. Runway's guide gives the example of changing "High angle of a koi fish pond" to "High angle looking down at a koi fish pond" to get the camera angle.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Runway is bad at","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Runway lists the weak spots itself. In its Gen-4.5 announcement from December 1, 2025, the company names errors in cause and effect, problems with object permanence, where things vanish or appear between frames, and success bias, where actions tend to work out even when they should not. Gen-4.5 output is also 720p, so upscaling costs an extra step.","sources":[{"name":"Runway: Introducing Runway Gen-4.5","url":"https://runway.com/research/introducing-runway-gen-4.5"},{"name":"Runway Help Center: Gen-4.5","url":"https://help.runwayml.com/hc/en-us/articles/46974685288467"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Gen-4.5 launched in first place on the Artificial Analysis Text to Video leaderboard, according to Runway, and it runs on NVIDIA GPUs. Benchmarks change fast, though, so treat a ranking as a reason to try it, not a promise.","sources":[{"name":"Runway: Introducing Runway Gen-4.5","url":"https://runway.com/research/introducing-runway-gen-4.5"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Runway is worth it if you make short clips often and want one place for images, video and edits. If you make one video a month, the one-time free credits and a careful Turbo test will tell you more than any review.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Gemini can now read your emails while you drive
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Google started rolling out the Gemini app on Apple CarPlay on November 11, worldwide, in every language Gemini Live supports. Tap the Gemini icon on the car's screen and talk to it hands-free. Using Gmail and Calendar, it can read your daily brief, sum up unread email and help you draft spoken replies. You can cut in mid-sentence or switch topics. Chats sync with the Gemini app on your iPhone. Gemini was the last major chatbot missing from CarPlay. ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, Copilot and Perplexity were already there. Sources: 9to5Google, Engadget, MacRumors, Digital Trends.

nf:hero.nf:alt: Gemini can now read your emails while you drive

It shows a waveform that indicates when Gemini is listening, thinking or responding, with End and Mute buttons in the top left corner, according to 9to5Google. As on the phone, drivers can interrupt Gemini Live mid-answer to add a detail, change the subject or pause the conversation.","sources":[{"name":"9to5Google","url":"https://9to5google.com/2026/11/11/gemini-app-carplay/"},{"name":"Digital Trends","url":"https://www.digitaltrends.com/computing/google-gemini-can-now-ride-along-in-your-car-and-catch-you-up-on-everything-you-missed/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Google's suggested uses include checking the day's calendar, hearing a daily brief, summarizing Gmail threads, finding places nearby and rehearsing a presentation on the drive. Digital Trends reported that, through Gmail and Calendar, Gemini can read out a daily brief, summarize unread email and help draft spoken replies. MacRumors gave the example of asking for a quick lunch spot in downtown Austin that is easy to get in and out of.","sources":[{"name":"9to5Google","url":"https://9to5google.com/2026/11/11/gemini-app-carplay/"},{"name":"MacRumors","url":"https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/11/google-gemini-apple-carplay/"},{"name":"Digital Trends","url":"https://www.digitaltrends.com/computing/google-gemini-can-now-ride-along-in-your-car-and-catch-you-up-on-everything-you-missed/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Conversations started in the car sync with the Gemini app on the iPhone and stay in the chat history, and drivers can resume a recent chat or start a new one. Google described the CarPlay version as designed to work like a conversational driving companion that minimizes distraction, according to 9to5Google.","sources":[{"name":"9to5Google","url":"https://9to5google.com/2026/11/11/gemini-app-carplay/"},{"name":"Engadget","url":"https://www.engadget.com/2314093/google-brings-the-gemini-app-to-apple-carplay/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to start","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Engadget and Digital Trends list three requirements: the latest version of the Gemini app on the iPhone, microphone permission turned on, and at least one earlier use of Gemini Live on the phone. After that, drivers tap the Gemini icon on the CarPlay screen. Digital Trends also noted that the Daily Brief feature has to be switched on before it can be used in the car.","sources":[{"name":"Engadget","url":"https://www.engadget.com/2314093/google-brings-the-gemini-app-to-apple-carplay/"},{"name":"Digital Trends","url":"https://www.digitaltrends.com/computing/google-gemini-can-now-ride-along-in-your-car-and-catch-you-up-on-everything-you-missed/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"CarPlay began supporting voice-based conversational AI apps with iOS 26.4, MacRumors reported. Gemini's main advantage there is its link to Gmail and Google Calendar, which lets it turn a commute into time for catching up on email and the day's schedule without touching the phone.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"Watch whether Google brings its Personal Intelligence features, which it is adding to Gemini on Android Auto and in cars with Google built-in, to the CarPlay app as well.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Canva AI: designs, slides and what each plan gets
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Tell Canva AI the format, the goal and the audience. It builds a full design you can edit. It works for social posts, presentations, websites, videos and docs. With a Brand Kit connected, Canva AI uses your colors, fonts and tone. Tag @Canva in a comment to get design feedback without writing a long prompt. Ask for one change, like a new headline or image. Canva says the rest of the design stays put. Sources: Canva Help Center: Understanding your AI usage, Canva Newsroom: Introducing Canva's Creative Operating System, 9to5Mac, Engadget, Fast Company, Tech Insider.

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use Canva AI: designs, presentations and what each plan gets","dek":"What Canva AI can build from one description, the steps that get a usable first draft, and how the monthly AI allowance works on each plan.","summary":"Canva AI turns a written description into a complete, editable design and can generate single elements, presentations and feedback. This guide walks through the steps and explains the monthly AI allowance, from up to 20 Premium uses on Canva Free to up to 400 on Business.","seo_title":"How to use Canva AI: designs, slides and limits by plan","seo_description":"How to use Canva AI step by step: describe a design, build a presentation, use your Brand Kit, three prompts to copy, and the AI limits on each plan.","answer_summary":"Describe the design you need to Canva AI, including the format, goal and audience, and it generates a complete design you can edit piece by piece. Every plan has a monthly AI allowance, which you can check by selecting your profile icon, then Settings, then Billing.","tags":["Canva","Canva AI","AI design","Presentations","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"How to use Canva AI comes down to three habits: describe the whole design instead of one picture, edit the result one element at a time, and keep an eye on your monthly AI allowance. Canva AI is the assistant built into Canva. You describe what you need in a chat, and it generates a design you can keep editing, according to Engadget and 9to5Mac's coverage of the Canva AI 2.0 launch in April 2026.","sources":[{"name":"9to5Mac","url":"https://9to5mac.com/2026/04/16/canva-ai-2-0-introduces-memory-connectors-and-automated-workflows/"},{"name":"Engadget","url":"https://www.engadget.com/ai/canva-starts-previewing-a-more-powerful-version-of-its-ai-assistant-130000966.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Canva says its own Canva Design Model now powers these features. The company describes it as a model trained on design structure, layering, hierarchy and branding, and says it creates fully editable content rather than a flat image. The same model is also available inside ChatGPT and Claude, Canva says.","sources":[{"name":"Canva Newsroom: Introducing Canva's Creative Operating System","url":"https://www.canva.com/newsroom/news/creative-operating-system/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Canva AI can make","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to Canva's newsroom, the main pieces are: AI-powered designs (a complete design for a social post, presentation, website, video or doc), AI-powered elements (photos, videos, icons, shapes, 3D elements and custom code from the Elements tab), Style Match (makes the look of a design consistent), Magic Background (a backdrop that fits the subject, layout and style), Guided Presentations, Magic Video and Ask @Canva, which gives feedback when you tag it in a comment.","sources":[{"name":"Canva Newsroom: Introducing Canva's Creative Operating System","url":"https://www.canva.com/newsroom/news/creative-operating-system/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Two newer models sit on top of that. Canva Craft, Canva's first image generation model, launched on October 22, 2026 in the Dream Lab tab and outputs images up to 2K, Tech Insider reported. Canva Brush, launched October 29, works through a design step by step and was available only to Canva Pro subscribers at launch, according to Fast Company.","sources":[{"name":"Fast Company","url":"https://www.fastcompany.com/91633207/could-canva-brush-new-ai-feature-end-graphic-design-slop"},{"name":"Tech Insider","url":"https://tech-insider.org/canva-craft-first-image-model-designarena-2026/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use Canva AI, step by step","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Start from the Canva AI chat","text":"Canva AI 2.0 is a conversational interface: you type what you need and it creates, edits and organizes the work. It launched as a research preview starting from the Canva homepage, with access widening over time, so the exact entry point can differ by account.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Describe the whole design, not one image","text":"Say the format, the goal, the audience and the tone in one message. Canva AI is built to generate a complete design with structure and layout, so a full brief gets you a usable first draft instead of a random picture.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: A social post from a brief","text":"Make an Instagram carousel of 5 slides announcing [event] on [date] at [place]. Audience: [who]. Tone: friendly and clear. Put the date and place on the first slide and a call to sign up on the last.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. For a deck, use Guided Presentations","text":"Canva says Guided Presentations is a conversational flow on the Canva AI homepage that first asks about your goal, then helps shape the story and structure the slides before you pick a layout. Answer its questions properly: the outline you agree on decides how good the slides are.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: A presentation outline","text":"I need a 10 slide presentation for [audience] about [topic]. The goal is to get them to [decision or action]. Use one idea per slide, end with a slide of next steps, and keep text under 25 words per slide.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Connect your Brand Kit","text":"Once a Brand Kit is connected, Canva AI generates designs that reflect the brand's colors, fonts, tone and style, according to Canva. Engadget also reported a brand tool that applies a company's visual identity to new and existing designs. Do this before you generate, not after.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Change one element at a time","text":"Canva AI 2.0 edits only the element you name, such as an image, a headline or a font, 9to5Mac reported. Ask for small, specific changes. If the parts of a design look mismatched, try Style Match; if the background looks empty, try Magic Background.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: A targeted fix","text":"Keep everything else the same. Replace the headline on slide 1 with a shorter one under 8 words, and make the photo on slide 3 warmer and brighter.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Ask @Canva for feedback","text":"Tag @Canva in a comment on your design. Canva says it gives design feedback and can generate visuals, using fonts, colors and tone that fit, without extra prompts.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Canva AI limits on each plan","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Every plan has one monthly AI allowance shared by Standard, Premium and Ultra tools, and Premium and Ultra tools use more of it per use. On Canva Free and Pro Lite, Standard tools count toward the allowance, with up to 20 Premium uses shared with Standard, and no Ultra tools. Canva Pro, Teams and Nonprofits get up to 200 Premium uses and up to 20 Ultra uses, and Standard tools such as Magic Write and Translate do not count. Business and Enterprise get up to 400 Premium and up to 40 Ultra uses.","sources":[{"name":"Canva Help Center: Understanding your AI usage","url":"https://www.canva.com/help/ai-access/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The numbers are a best case. Canva says they assume simple prompts and the cheapest tool in each category, and that Canva AI 2.0 conversational design uses more than single prompt features, rising with the size of the design, the complexity of the task and the model needed. Designs made through ChatGPT or Claude connected to Canva also draw from your allowance.","sources":[{"name":"Canva Help Center: Understanding your AI usage","url":"https://www.canva.com/help/ai-access/"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"To see what is left, select your profile icon, then Settings, then Billing, and look under AI usage. Free allowances reset at midnight UTC on the first of each month; paid plans reset on the billing date.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"When you run out on Free, Canva adds short pauses between Standard and Premium generations and blocks Ultra tools until the reset. You can upgrade, buy an AI Pass or a top-up where your plan allows it, or wait.","sources":[{"name":"Canva Help Center: Understanding your AI usage","url":"https://www.canva.com/help/ai-access/"},{"name":"Engadget","url":"https://www.engadget.com/ai/canva-starts-previewing-a-more-powerful-version-of-its-ai-assistant-130000966.html"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where Canva AI falls short","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The allowance is the real limit. Chat-style editing is the most useful part of Canva AI and also the most expensive per request, so a long back and forth on a big deck can use far more of a Free month than the headline number suggests. Some of the newest tools, like Brush, started on paid plans only, and the AI 2.0 assistant rolled out gradually, so not every account sees the same features at the same time. Treat the first draft as a layout to edit, check every fact and number in it yourself, and spend your AI uses on the changes that would take longest by hand.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Kling AI to make videos, and what is really free
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Kling sells credits at $1 for 66. Failed runs are refunded. A 5 second 720p clip with no audio costs 30 credits on VIDEO 3.0. Label shots in order: framing, camera move, action. Mark moments like "At the 3rd second" and give each line of dialogue a speaker and tone. The Multi-Shot switch lets the model plan the cuts. Sources: Kling AI: Credits policy, Kling AI: VIDEO 3.0 model user guide, Atlas Cloud: How to get Kling AI free credits, Kling AI: VIDEO 3.0 Omni model user guide, Let's Data Science: Kling AI opens Kling 4.0.

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use Kling AI to make videos (free credits explained)","dek":"What the free account really gives you, what each second costs, and three prompt patterns from Kling's own guide.","summary":"Kling AI charges credits for every second of video, at $1 for 66 credits, and refunds failed runs. This guide explains the free credits, the cost per clip, and how to make your first video step by step.","seo_title":"How to use Kling AI to make videos (free credits explained)","seo_description":"How to use Kling AI step by step: free credits, what each video costs, three prompts to copy, Multi-Shot, and what Kling 4.0 adds.","answer_summary":"Sign in at kling.ai, check your credits in the left sidebar, start from text or an image, pick 3 to 15 seconds and 720p or 1080p, and write the prompt as a shot list. A 5 second 720p clip without audio costs 30 credits on Kling VIDEO 3.0.","tags":["Kling AI","AI video","Kuaishou","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"How to use Kling AI to make videos comes down to three things: knowing what the free account really gives you, writing prompts the way Kling's own guide asks for, and checking the credit cost before every clip. Kling is an AI video generator from Kuaishou that turns text, images and video references into short clips with sound.","sources":[{"name":"Kling AI: VIDEO 3.0 model user guide","url":"https://kling.ai/quickstart/klingai-video-3-model-user-guide"},{"name":"Let's Data Science: Kling AI opens Kling 4.0","url":"https://letsdatascience.com/news/kling-ai-opens-kling-40-to-all-users-d9dc6422"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The quick version: credits are Kling's currency, a video costs credits for every second you generate, and failed generations are refunded. Kling sells credits at a standard rate of $1 for 66 credits. A 5 second clip at 720p without audio costs 30 credits on the Kling VIDEO 3.0 model, according to Kling's own user guide.","sources":[{"name":"Kling AI: Credits policy","url":"https://kling.ai/docs/point-policy"},{"name":"Kling AI: VIDEO 3.0 model user guide","url":"https://kling.ai/quickstart/klingai-video-3-model-user-guide"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Kling AI free credits explained","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Kling's credit policy lists several kinds of credits: promotional credits from events, monthly credits that come with a membership and last one month, credits from a 7 day membership, daily login credits that subscribers can claim during events, and purchased credits that stay valid for two years. When you generate, Kling spends the credits that expire soonest first.","sources":[{"name":"Kling AI: Credits policy","url":"https://kling.ai/docs/point-policy"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The policy does not promise a fixed free allowance. A third-party guide from Atlas Cloud, published July 14, 2026, says the free plan gets 66 credits on the first login of each month, valid for one month, which is enough for about two 5 second clips at 720p. Treat that number as a guide, not a promise, and check your own balance.","sources":[{"name":"Kling AI: Credits policy","url":"https://kling.ai/docs/point-policy"},{"name":"Atlas Cloud: How to get Kling AI free credits","url":"https://www.atlascloud.ai/blog/tips/kling-ai-free"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Some features are paid only. Kling's policy names fast-track generation, 1080p video, watermark removal, master shot and video extension, and image upscaling as premium features that credits alone do not unlock. Atlas Cloud adds that free output carries a watermark and that the free queue can be too busy to accept new tasks at peak times.","sources":[{"name":"Kling AI: Credits policy","url":"https://kling.ai/docs/point-policy"},{"name":"Atlas Cloud: How to get Kling AI free credits","url":"https://www.atlascloud.ai/blog/tips/kling-ai-free"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"To see how many credits you have, click the remaining credits number in the left sidebar on the Kling website. Do this before you start, not after a failed run.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How much a Kling AI video costs in credits","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Kling's VIDEO 3.0 guide charges per second. With Native Audio on, it costs 12 credits a second at 1080p and 9 at 720p. With No Native Audio, it costs 8 credits a second at 1080p and 6 at 720p. Voice control adds 2 credits a second. So a 5 second 1080p clip with sound costs 60 credits, and the same clip with voice control costs 70.","sources":[{"name":"Kling AI: VIDEO 3.0 model user guide","url":"https://kling.ai/quickstart/klingai-video-3-model-user-guide"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The VIDEO 3.0 Omni model, which can also take a video as a reference, costs 16 credits a second at 1080p and 12 at 720p when you add a video input, with native audio off. Clips on both 3.0 models run from 3 to 15 seconds.","sources":[{"name":"Kling AI: VIDEO 3.0 model user guide","url":"https://kling.ai/quickstart/klingai-video-3-model-user-guide"},{"name":"Kling AI: VIDEO 3.0 Omni model user guide","url":"https://kling.ai/quickstart/klingai-video-3-omni-model-user-guide"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to make your first Kling AI video","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Log in and check your balance","text":"Go to kling.ai and sign in. Credits only work for logged-in users. Click the credits number in the left sidebar so you know your budget.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Choose how to start","text":"Kling VIDEO 3.0 supports text to video, image to video, and video from a start frame and an end frame. If you have a still you like, start from the image: you only describe the motion, and you waste fewer runs on a look you did not want.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Pick length, resolution and audio","text":"Set a length between 3 and 15 seconds and choose 720p or 1080p. Choose Native Audio if you want sound and speech, or No Native Audio to save credits. For a test, use 720p without audio and keep it short.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Write the prompt like a shot list","text":"Kling's guide asks you to label shots in order and describe framing and camera movement for each one. You can mark timed moments, give every line of dialogue a speaker and a tone, and ask for an accent.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: One clean shot","text":"A single unbroken shot with no edited transitions. Slow push-in on [subject] in [place] at [time of day], soft light from the left, shallow depth of field. At the 3rd second, [subject] turns and looks at the camera.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: A short multi-shot scene","text":"Shot 1, wide shot of [person] walking into [place], cinematic handheld.\nShot 2, close-up of [person]'s face as they notice [thing].\n[Person] (softly, in a surprised tone): [one short line of dialogue].","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Text that must stay readable","text":"The camera remains fixed on the word \"[WORD]\" printed on [object], then slowly pulls back to show [scene].","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Use Multi-Shot when you need cuts","text":"In the VIDEO 3.0 input area, turn on the Multi-Shot switch and the model plans the shots itself. Then click Custom Multi-Shot to set the number of shots, how long each one runs and what happens in each.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Keep a character the same across clips","text":"Upload an image and use Bind Subject to Enhance Consistency, or build an element from 2 to 4 reference images. For a talking character, you can upload a short video to create a character element with its own voice.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Kling 4.0 changes","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Kuaishou says Kling 4.0 launched on October 15, 2026, after early access from September 30. The company says it makes clips of up to 30 seconds in one pass, accepts up to 15 reference assets and up to 10 keyframes, and can be used by AI agents through a Kling MCP and command line tool. Kuaishou did not publish 4.0 prices in that announcement, so check the cost on your own screen before you try it.","sources":[{"name":"Let's Data Science: Kling AI opens Kling 4.0","url":"https://letsdatascience.com/news/kling-ai-opens-kling-40-to-all-users-d9dc6422"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where Kling AI falls short","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Kling is strong at short, controlled shots with sound, and its prompt guide is unusually specific. The weak spot is cost. Every re-roll spends credits, 1080p and watermark removal sit behind a paid plan, and a free monthly allowance of about two short clips leaves very little room to experiment. Draft at 720p without audio, then spend on the version you keep.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Long prompts do not save a bad idea. One clear subject, one camera move and one action per shot will beat a paragraph of adjectives. If a generation fails, check your balance: Kling says failed generations are refunded.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Kling translates prompts in unsupported languages into English. Its 3.0 guide lists five supported languages for speech: Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean and Spanish.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Higgsfield AI, and what you really get for free
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: No free trial. The free tier gives a small set of models and no credits. Paid plans add monthly credits, more models and Unlimited access to some models on mid and top plans. Open AI Video, press Create Video Now and choose Kling, Seedance, Veo or another model. Sources: Higgsfield Help Center: How do Higgsfield plans work, Higgsfield Help Center: How do credits work, Higgsfield Help Center: Unlimited models, Higgsfield Help Center: What uses my credits, Higgsfield: AI video generator, Higgsfield: About, Layer3Labs: How to use Higgsfield.

Everything below tells you what you can do for free, how to make your first video, and how not to burn credits by accident.","sources":[{"name":"Higgsfield Help Center: How do Higgsfield plans work","url":"https://higgsfield.ai/creator-hub/help-center/plans-and-subscriptions/how-do-higgsfield-plans-work"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What you get on Higgsfield for free","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Higgsfield says you can generate on the free tier with a limited set of models and upgrade later.
