Reuters said that with all of these cornerstone investments included, the total offering could raise up to $90.4 billion. Anthropic also expects to give underwriters a 30 day option to buy up to 123.75 million additional shares.","sources":[{"name":"Reuters","url":"https://lufkindailynews.com/news_reuters/business/anthropic-ipo-to-raise-up-to-64-4-billion-as-ai-boom-faces-growing-scrutiny/article_84186764-e804-5f5d-ae55-4fd6a8a166dc.html"},{"name":"Anthropic","url":"https://www.anthropic.com/news/roadshow-launch"},{"name":"RTTNews","url":"https://www.rttnews.com/3712632/anthropic-sets-ipo-price-range-at-70-78-per-share-launches-roadshow.aspx"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The filing shows fast growth and heavy spending. Third quarter revenue rose 47% from the prior quarter to $16.96 billion, Reuters reported, a slowdown from growth of 144% in the quarter before. Commitments for computing power total about $900 billion, including deals with Amazon and Google. A separate Reuters analysis said revenue in the first half of 2026 reached $16.29 billion, about 14 times the level a year earlier.","sources":[{"name":"Reuters","url":"https://lufkindailynews.com/news_reuters/business/anthropic-ipo-to-raise-up-to-64-4-billion-as-ai-boom-faces-growing-scrutiny/article_84186764-e804-5f5d-ae55-4fd6a8a166dc.html"},{"name":"RTTNews","url":"https://www.rttnews.com/3712632/anthropic-sets-ipo-price-range-at-70-78-per-share-launches-roadshow.aspx"},{"name":"Reuters via Investing.com","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/anthropics-ipo-a-close-look-at-ai-frontrunners-rapid-growth-spiraling-costs-5015034"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The listing comes at a difficult moment for technology stocks. Reuters noted that the Nasdaq had its deepest one day drop in 19 months on the Thursday before the roadshow, amid scrutiny of AI spending after Democratic gains in the midterm elections. The prospectus warns that rivals could gain an edge by building models faster and that advances in AI could outpace safety measures.","sources":[{"name":"Reuters","url":"https://lufkindailynews.com/news_reuters/business/anthropic-ipo-to-raise-up-to-64-4-billion-as-ai-boom-faces-growing-scrutiny/article_84186764-e804-5f5d-ae55-4fd6a8a166dc.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Anthropic was founded in 2021 by former OpenAI researchers, including chief executive Dario Amodei and his sister Daniela Amodei, and makes the Claude family of models. It is a public benefit corporation, and Reuters reported that a single Class F share controlled by its seven co-founders carries 50.1% of the voting power on key matters.","sources":[{"name":"Reuters","url":"https://lufkindailynews.com/news_reuters/business/anthropic-ipo-to-raise-up-to-64-4-billion-as-ai-boom-faces-growing-scrutiny/article_84186764-e804-5f5d-ae55-4fd6a8a166dc.html"},{"name":"Reuters via Investing.com","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/anthropics-ipo-a-close-look-at-ai-frontrunners-rapid-growth-spiraling-costs-5015034"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The range is a compromise. At the top end the valuation sits only slightly above the last private round, which suggests Anthropic chose a price that public investors can accept after weeks of pressure on AI stocks rather than chasing the higher figures discussed earlier in the year. The $26 billion from suppliers and cloud partners gives the deal a large base of committed demand before the order book opens.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"The final price, set at the end of the roadshow, will show whether demand pushed Anthropic toward the top of the $70 to $78 range or forced it lower, a signal for every AI company planning to go public.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Anthropic sent bankers its IPO price. Then took it back
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: On November 9, Anthropic sent bankers a filing pricing its IPO at $70 to $80 a share, Reuters reported. A second email said the pricing was "inaccurate" and a new filing would follow. It did not say what was wrong. The filing listed about 867 million shares. At $80 each, that raises $69.3 billion. One analyst put the implied value near $1.4 trillion. Investors once talked about $2 trillion. The filing also showed $26 billion from Google, Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft and TSMC. Sources: Reuters, Stocktwits, Business Standard.

nf:hero.nf:alt: Dario Amodei with a serious expression, photographed in front of a plain background.

item.nf:article: {"headline":"Anthropic retracts IPO price range it sent to bankers","dek":"The Claude maker said the $70 to $80 per share figures were inaccurate and promised an updated filing.","summary":"Anthropic sent bankers an IPO filing pricing shares at $70 to $80, a raise of up to $69.3 billion, then called the figures inaccurate, Reuters reported. An updated filing is expected before trading starts.","seo_title":"Anthropic IPO: price range of $70 to $80 retracted","seo_description":"Anthropic sent bankers IPO terms of $70 to $80 a share, up to $69.3 billion, then said the pricing was inaccurate. What the filing showed and what comes next.","answer_summary":"Anthropic briefly circulated an IPO price range of $70 to $80 per share on November 9, 2026, then told bankers the figures were inaccurate. It said an updated filing would follow.","tags":["Anthropic","IPO","Claude","Dario Amodei","Stock market"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Anthropic sent bankers a copy of a securities filing on November 9, 2026, that priced its planned initial public offering at $70 to $80 per share, then retracted the pricing hours later, according to a Reuters report based on emails the news agency reviewed.","sources":[{"name":"Reuters","url":"https://www.marketscreener.com/news/anthropic-s-nearly-70-billion-ipo-plan-briefly-circulated-to-banks-then-retracted-ce785edad988fe23"},{"name":"Business Standard","url":"https://www.business-standard.com/amp/world-news/anthropic-retracts-69-3-bn-ipo-figures-says-revised-details-to-follow-126111000143_1.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"A follow-up email from the company told the same recipients that the pricing details were inaccurate and that an updated filing would come later. The email did not explain what was wrong, and Reuters said it could not determine the error. Anthropic declined to comment to Reuters.","sources":[{"name":"Reuters","url":"https://www.marketscreener.com/news/anthropic-s-nearly-70-billion-ipo-plan-briefly-circulated-to-banks-then-retracted-ce785edad988fe23"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What the original filing showed","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The retracted version listed about 866.7 million Class A shares. Anthropic itself would sell roughly 843.3 million of them, and existing shareholders would sell about 23.3 million in a secondary offering. At the top of the price range, the sale would raise $69.3 billion, Reuters reported.","sources":[{"name":"Reuters","url":"https://www.marketscreener.com/news/anthropic-s-nearly-70-billion-ipo-plan-briefly-circulated-to-banks-then-retracted-ce785edad988fe23"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Shay Boloor of Futurum Equities estimated that the share count and price range implied a valuation of about $1.4 trillion, according to Stocktwits. Nasdaq Private Market currently values the company at $1.46 trillion, the same report said.","sources":[{"name":"Stocktwits","url":"https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/anthropic-retracts-reported-70-80-ipo-price-range-says-pricing-update-is-coming-listing-expected-next-week/cNGud3sR970"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The filing also described $26 billion in commitments from large technology companies alongside the IPO. Alphabet's Google, Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Micron Technology, Microsoft and TSMC agreed to buy Class N common stock in a private placement at the IPO price, closing right after the offering, according to Reuters.","sources":[{"name":"Reuters","url":"https://www.marketscreener.com/news/anthropic-s-nearly-70-billion-ipo-plan-briefly-circulated-to-banks-then-retracted-ce785edad988fe23"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"A falling valuation and a tight schedule","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Investors had earlier discussed a valuation of up to $2 trillion for the Claude developer. Reuters previously reported that $1.5 trillion is now seen as the high end, and Bloomberg reported talk of roughly $1.1 trillion to $1.3 trillion, according to Business Standard. Some potential investors wanted a better price before committing after a sharp sell-off in AI stocks following the US midterm elections.","sources":[{"name":"Reuters","url":"https://www.marketscreener.com/news/anthropic-s-nearly-70-billion-ipo-plan-briefly-circulated-to-banks-then-retracted-ce785edad988fe23"},{"name":"Business Standard","url":"https://www.business-standard.com/amp/world-news/anthropic-retracts-69-3-bn-ipo-figures-says-revised-details-to-follow-126111000143_1.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Reuters said a formal roadshow was expected to start on Tuesday, November 10, with pricing the following week. The Wall Street Journal reported that Anthropic has investor meetings this week and aims to begin trading on Thursday or Friday of next week, though the company could still delay, Stocktwits noted.","sources":[{"name":"Reuters","url":"https://www.marketscreener.com/news/anthropic-s-nearly-70-billion-ipo-plan-briefly-circulated-to-banks-then-retracted-ce785edad988fe23"},{"name":"Stocktwits","url":"https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/anthropic-retracts-reported-70-80-ipo-price-range-says-pricing-update-is-coming-listing-expected-next-week/cNGud3sR970"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The offering comes as other AI infrastructure and data center companies have delayed or withdrawn listings amid rising interest rates, and as shares and bonds of operators such as CoreWeave have sold off, Reuters reported.","sources":[{"name":"Reuters","url":"https://www.marketscreener.com/news/anthropic-s-nearly-70-billion-ipo-plan-briefly-circulated-to-banks-then-retracted-ce785edad988fe23"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"The numbers behind the company","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Anthropic reported revenue of almost $17 billion for the three months ended September 30 in an amended filing earlier in November. Stocktwits, citing that filing, put third quarter growth at about 47 percent from the previous quarter, down from 144 percent in the second quarter, with a net loss of $23.29 billion for the period.","sources":[{"name":"Reuters","url":"https://www.marketscreener.com/news/anthropic-s-nearly-70-billion-ipo-plan-briefly-circulated-to-banks-then-retracted-ce785edad988fe23"},{"name":"Stocktwits","url":"https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/anthropic-retracts-reported-70-80-ipo-price-range-says-pricing-update-is-coming-listing-expected-next-week/cNGud3sR970"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The company has nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including Amazon and Google, Reuters reported. Stocktwits put the total at $895.4 billion stretching to 2045, against about $146.6 billion in cash and other liquid assets.","sources":[{"name":"Reuters","url":"https://www.marketscreener.com/news/anthropic-s-nearly-70-billion-ipo-plan-briefly-circulated-to-banks-then-retracted-ce785edad988fe23"},{"name":"Stocktwits","url":"https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/anthropic-retracts-reported-70-80-ipo-price-range-says-pricing-update-is-coming-listing-expected-next-week/cNGud3sR970"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"A pulled price range is unusual for an offering of this size, and it lands at a sensitive moment. The figures in the retracted email were close to the valuation investors have been discussing, so the correction may be minor, but until the new filing appears the market has no official number to anchor on. The $26 billion placement from chip and cloud suppliers also shows how closely Anthropic's largest partners are tied to the outcome.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"The next item to watch is Anthropic's updated filing with a corrected price range, which will show whether the company is still aiming near $1.4 trillion or has moved lower before trading begins.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Nano Banana in Gemini for free: 5 prompts that work
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: undefined... Sources: Gemini Apps Help: Generate and edit images, Google Gemini: AI image generator and photo editor, Google: Nano Banana 2 announcement, Engadget, Tom's Guide.
item.category: Gemini Apps Help: Generate and edit images
Google Gemini: AI image generator and photo editor

nf:hero.nf:alt: A Google Pixel phone with the Gemini app open on its screen.

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use Gemini Nano Banana for free: edit and create images","dek":"Nano Banana 2 is the image model inside the free Gemini app. Here is how to make a picture, edit your own photo and get better results with prompts you can copy.","summary":"Nano Banana 2 is Google's default image model in the Gemini app and the free choice for creating and editing pictures. Paid Google AI plans add Nano Banana Pro and higher limits.","seo_title":"How to use Gemini Nano Banana for free: edit and create images","seo_description":"How to use Nano Banana in Gemini for free: make images, edit your own photos, merge pictures, download them, plus 6 prompts to copy and the limits to know.","answer_summary":"Go to gemini.google.com, open the sidebar, choose Images and type a prompt that starts with a verb. To edit a photo, upload it and describe the change. Nano Banana 2 is the free default model.","tags":["Gemini","Nano Banana","Google","AI images","AI guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"If you want to know how to use Gemini Nano Banana for free, the short answer is that you already have it. Nano Banana 2 is the default image model in the Gemini app, and Google's product page describes it as the free model for making and editing images. Google introduced it on February 26, 2026, built on Gemini 3.1 Flash Image, and said it replaced Nano Banana Pro across the Fast, Thinking and Pro modes in the app.","sources":[{"name":"Google Gemini: AI image generator and photo editor","url":"https://gemini.google/gb/overview/image-generation/?hl=en-GB"},{"name":"Google: Nano Banana 2 announcement","url":"https://dev.to/googleai/nano-banana-2-combining-pro-capabilities-with-lightning-fast-speed-4fm1"},{"name":"Engadget","url":"https://www.engadget.com/ai/googles-nano-banana-2-is-a-faster-version-of-nano-banana-pro-160000695.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"It does two jobs. It creates new pictures from a text prompt, and it edits pictures you upload: change a background, swap an object, add something, or combine several photos into one. Google lists better text inside images, consistent characters across images and edits to one part of a photo as its main strengths.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Generate and edit images","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/14286560?hl=en&co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop"},{"name":"Google Gemini: AI image generator and photo editor","url":"https://gemini.google/gb/overview/image-generation/?hl=en-GB"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What you need before you start","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"You need a Google account signed in to Gemini. Google's help page says image editing is not available to users under 18, and the feature is limited to the countries and languages where the Gemini app works. Work and school accounts can have different rules or no access at all.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Generate and edit images","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/14286560?hl=en&co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The free plan has a daily limit. Google does not publish the exact number on its help page; it only says that limits apply and that paid Google AI plans get higher ones. Paid subscribers can also redo an image with Nano Banana Pro, the slower model meant for images that need more detail and more precise control.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Generate and edit images","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/14286560?hl=en&co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop"},{"name":"Google Gemini: AI image generator and photo editor","url":"https://gemini.google/gb/overview/image-generation/?hl=en-GB"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to make your first image with Nano Banana","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Open Gemini","text":"Go to gemini.google.com on a computer, or open the Gemini app on your phone, and sign in.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Open Images","text":"On the web, click Open Sidebar, then Images. You can pick one of the ready-made templates or type your own prompt.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Write the prompt","text":"Start with a verb such as create, draw or generate. Then say the style, the subject, what the subject is doing and where. One clear sentence beats a list of keywords.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Download it","text":"Hover over the finished image and click Download full size. You can also click More under the image and choose Export to Docs if you want to keep working on it in a document.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The model you pick in Gemini decides which image model runs. According to Google's help page, Flash-Lite uses Nano Banana 2 Lite, which is quick but not made for several reference images or repeated edits. Flash and Pro use Nano Banana 2. So for editing work, switch away from Flash-Lite before you ask for the image.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Generate and edit images","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/14286560?hl=en&co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to edit your own photo","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Upload the picture","text":"Start a chat in Gemini and add your photo with the upload button. You can add several pictures at once if you want Gemini to combine them.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Describe only the change","text":"Say what should stay the same and what should change. Be concrete: which object, which side of the picture, which color.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Keep editing in the same chat","text":"Ask for one fix at a time. For an image you made earlier, open Library in the sidebar, click the image, click Chat under it and type the next change.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Tom's Guide reported in December 2025 that the Gemini app lets you draw or circle on an uploaded photo to mark the spot you want changed, with or without a text prompt. Google's help page does not describe this tool, so if you do not see it, describe the spot in words instead.","sources":[{"name":"Tom's Guide","url":"https://www.tomsguide.com/ai/ai-image-video/nano-banana-now-lets-you-draw-prompts-directly-on-your-photos-sam-altman-is-going-to-hate-this"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Gemini Nano Banana prompts to copy","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: A clean first image","text":"Create a photorealistic image of [subject] [doing what] in [place], [time of day] light, shot from [angle].","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Fix one part of a photo","text":"Keep everything in this photo exactly the same, but replace [the thing to change] with [the new thing]. Do not change the faces.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Combine photos","text":"Put the person from the first image and the [pet or object] from the second image together in the setting from the third image. Natural lighting, same style as the third image.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Text that reads right","text":"Design a [poster, invitation or card] that says \"[exact words]\" in large letters, with \"[smaller line]\" below it. Style: [watercolor, retro, minimal]. Background: [color].","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: Borrow a style","text":"Apply the colors, texture and mood of the second image to the subject in the first image. Keep the subject's shape and face unchanged.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 6: A new format","text":"Turn this image into a [9:16 vertical, 16:9 wide or square] version. Extend the background naturally and keep the subject centered.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Google's own page lists changing the mood, lighting, camera angle or focus of a photo, and adjusting a picture to a different aspect ratio, as things the model handles. Those make good first experiments because the result is easy to judge.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where Nano Banana needs help","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Google's help page itself points to the weak spots: the Lite model is not built for several references or repeated edits, and the free plan has a daily cap. In practice that means short, specific requests work best. Split a big edit into steps, tell the model what to keep as well as what to change, and when a result is close, ask for one fix instead of starting over so you do not spend your daily images.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Every image is marked as AI-made. Google says each picture carries an invisible SynthID watermark and a visible watermark, and that you can upload an image to the Gemini app and ask whether Google AI made it. Google may also remove images whose prompts break its terms or its prohibited use policy.","sources":[{"name":"Google Gemini: AI image generator and photo editor","url":"https://gemini.google/gb/overview/image-generation/?hl=en-GB"},{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Generate and edit images","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/14286560?hl=en&co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If you pay for a Google AI plan and an image needs finer detail or cleaner text, click More at the bottom right of the image and choose Redo with Pro. Free users stay on Nano Banana 2.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Nano Banana 2 is not only in the Gemini app. Google said it is also the default in AI Mode and Lens in Search and in its Flow creative studio, where it costs zero credits, and Engadget noted it can keep the look of up to five characters consistent in one workflow.","sources":[{"name":"Google: Nano Banana 2 announcement","url":"https://dev.to/googleai/nano-banana-2-combining-pro-capabilities-with-lightning-fast-speed-4fm1"},{"name":"Engadget","url":"https://www.engadget.com/ai/googles-nano-banana-2-is-a-faster-version-of-nano-banana-pro-160000695.html"}]}]}

item.title: ChatGPT image prompts that actually work: 5 tricks for better pictures and edits
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: undefined... Sources: OpenAI: Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.5, OpenAI Developer Community: Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.6, RuntimeWire, DataCamp.
item.category: OpenAI Developer Community: Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.6

nf:hero.nf:alt: ChatGPT image prompts that actually work: 5 tricks for better pictures and edits

item.nf:article:
{"kind":"guide","headline":"ChatGPT Images: how to write image prompts and edit pictures that come out right","dek":"ChatGPT can now change one part of a picture and leave the rest alone. Here is how to prompt it, edit with it and turn images into GIFs.","summary":"ChatGPT Images 2.5 and 2.6 make targeted edits, follow rough sketches and can turn a picture into an animated GIF. The best results come from saying what must stay the same, changing one thing per request and marking unknown details as placeholders.","seo_title":"ChatGPT Images: prompts and editing tips that work","seo_description":"How to write ChatGPT image prompts, make targeted edits, use @Sketch and templates, and turn pictures into GIFs with Images 2.6. Prompts to copy.","answer_summary":"Describe the image you want, then edit in small steps: say what must stay the same and change one thing per request. Type @Sketch to draw a layout, and use a picture or prompt to make a GIF.","tags":["ChatGPT","OpenAI","AI images","Prompts","AI guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"ChatGPT makes and edits pictures right inside a chat. Since Images 2.5 arrived on September 8, 2026, OpenAI says edits change only what you ask for and keep the rest of the image intact, and earlier edits tend to stick across a long conversation. Images 2.5 rolled out to all ChatGPT tiers on desktop, mobile and web.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI: Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.5","url":"https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-images-2-5/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Images 2.6 followed on November 4, 2026. It adds animated GIFs and reference images you save once and reuse, and it is available across all subscription tiers on desktop, mobile and web, according to OpenAI's announcement and RuntimeWire.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Developer Community: Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.6","url":"https://community.openai.com/t/images-upgraded-introducing-chatgpt-images-2-6/1412901"},{"name":"RuntimeWire","url":"https://runtimewire.com/article/openai-chatgpt-images-2-6-gifs-flare-sunburst-api"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The short version of this guide: describe the picture, then fix it in small steps. Say what must stay the same, change one thing per message, and use a sketch when words are not enough. The prompts below are ready to copy.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI: Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.5","url":"https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-images-2-5/"},{"name":"DataCamp","url":"https://www.datacamp.com/blog/chatgpt-images-2-5"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Start with a clear first prompt","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Write the subject first, then the setting, then the style and light. You do not need a long paragraph. A clear sentence or two beats a list of twenty adjectives, because every extra word is one more thing the model has to balance.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: A clean first image","text":"A close-up photo of a ceramic coffee mug on a wooden kitchen table, morning sunlight from a window on the left, soft shadows, calm and warm.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenAI's own example for Images 2.5 shows the style it handles well: concrete details about what a person wears and what surrounds them. Its sample prompt for a 1980s portrait begins with a smiling man with curly hair in a teal, navy and pink windbreaker and a gold chain, then adds the lights and a boombox.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI: Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.5","url":"https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-images-2-5/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Edit in small steps","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Editing is where the tool is strongest. DataCamp's hands-on test found that local edits, such as a new background, a changed line of text or one swapped object, work best, and that the rest of the picture holds up when the change is small and targeted. Moving several objects at once or re-posing a person can break consistency and leave artifacts outside the edited area.","sources":[{"name":"DataCamp","url":"https://www.datacamp.com/blog/chatgpt-images-2-5"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Upload your photo or start from a generated image","text":"Add the picture to the chat, or make one with a first prompt.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Name what must not change","text":"If a face, a logo or a product shape matters, say so in the same message as the edit.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Keep the person, change the scene","text":"Change only the background to a quiet beach at sunset. Keep my face, hairstyle, clothes and pose exactly the same.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Ask for one change per message","text":"Treat each follow-up as its own small request. If the date on a poster is wrong, ask to change that date, not to redo the whole poster.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: One fix at a time","text":"Change the date on the poster to [NEW DATE]. Do not change anything else.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"You can also point at the exact spot. OpenAI says Images 2.5 lets you place comments directly on an image for focused edits, so the model knows which area you mean without a long description.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI: Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.5","url":"https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-images-2-5/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Use @Sketch and templates","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Type @Sketch in ChatGPT to draw directly in the chat and use the drawing as a guide. OpenAI says adding a style description helps. DataCamp found a sketch most useful for spatial details, such as where two characters stand, that are awkward to put into words. You do not need to draw well.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI: Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.5","url":"https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-images-2-5/"},{"name":"DataCamp","url":"https://www.datacamp.com/blog/chatgpt-images-2-5"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Sketch to finished picture","text":"@Sketch Turn my drawing into a children's book illustration: a small fox on the left, a big tree on the right, soft pastel colors.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Templates give you a starting format such as Poster or Merch. You then add the content, the design elements and the style, OpenAI says. They are good for repeat formats, though DataCamp notes they leave less room for open-ended ideas.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI: Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.5","url":"https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-images-2-5/"},{"name":"DataCamp","url":"https://www.datacamp.com/blog/chatgpt-images-2-5"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: A poster with placeholders","text":"Poster for a neighborhood yard sale. Friendly, bright colors, hand-drawn feel.
Title: Yard Sale
Date: [DATE]
Address: [ADDRESS]
Leave space at the bottom for a small map.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Mark anything you do not know yet with brackets, like [DATE]. DataCamp's tests suggest giving the event details and the mood, then marking unknowns as placeholders, so you can fill them in later with a one-line edit.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Reuse faces and make GIFs","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"With Images 2.6 you can save reference images of yourself, your pets and recurring characters and reuse them without uploading them again, OpenAI says. You can also turn a prompt or an image into an animated GIF, then adjust the speed and edit individual frames before you share it.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Developer Community: Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.6","url":"https://community.openai.com/t/images-upgraded-introducing-chatgpt-images-2-6/1412901"},{"name":"RuntimeWire","url":"https://runtimewire.com/article/openai-chatgpt-images-2-6-gifs-flare-sunburst-api"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 6: A reaction GIF","text":"Make a short looping GIF of my saved cat character waking up, stretching and yawning. Simple, clean background.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What it still gets wrong","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Text is still a weak spot, especially small or dense type. Hair edges in portrait edits can look rough, and results can still have a recognizable AI look, according to DataCamp's review. Every image carries C2PA metadata and an invisible watermark that marks it as made with OpenAI tools, the company says.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI: Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.5","url":"https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-images-2-5/"},{"name":"DataCamp","url":"https://www.datacamp.com/blog/chatgpt-images-2-5"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If a long edit starts drifting, do not keep stacking fixes. Go back to the last good version, restate what must stay the same, and make the next change on its own.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Midjourney prompts that actually work: 5 rules from its own docs
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: undefined... Sources: Midjourney Docs: Prompt Basics, Midjourney Docs: Parameter List, Midjourney Docs: Models, Midjourney Docs: Getting Started Guide, Visually AI (Heather Cooper): Midjourney V8 is live on alpha, Evolink: Midjourney V8.1 prompt guide.
item.category: Visually AI (Heather Cooper): Midjourney V8 is live on alpha

nf:hero.nf:alt: A lone figure stands before a large glacier over dark water under a stormy sky.

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"Midjourney prompts: how to write image prompts that work","dek":"Midjourney rewards short, precise prompts and a few settings placed at the end. Here is what its own documentation recommends, with prompts to copy.","summary":"Midjourney's documentation says short, simple prompts usually produce the best images, with exact numbers, precise words and only the details you care about. Settings such as aspect ratio go at the end of the prompt, and the --no parameter removes things you do not want.","seo_title":"Midjourney prompts: how to write image prompts that work","seo_description":"Write better Midjourney prompts: keep them short, use exact numbers, pick the details that matter, put parameters at the end and remove things with --no.","answer_summary":"Write a short description of the image you want with precise words and exact numbers, add only the details that matter (subject, medium, setting, lighting, color, mood, composition), then put parameters like --ar 16:9 at the end.","tags":["Midjourney","AI images","Prompts","Image generation","AI guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Midjourney turns a written description into images. You type a prompt into the Imagine bar on the Create page at midjourney.com, press Enter, and it makes a set of four images. You need a paid plan before you can make your first image, according to Midjourney's Getting Started Guide.","sources":[{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Getting Started Guide","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/hc/en-us/articles/33329261836941-Getting-Started-Guide"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The short version of this guide: write less than you think, choose exact words, say how many of something you want, describe what should be in the picture rather than what should not, and put settings at the very end. Everything below comes from Midjourney's own documentation, plus notes from people who test new versions.","sources":[{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Prompt Basics","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/prompts"},{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Parameter List","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/parameter-list"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Start with a short prompt","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Midjourney's Prompt Basics page is blunt about length. Short, simple prompts usually produce the best images. It suggests thinking of a prompt as a quick snapshot of the idea, and it warns that long lists and detailed instructions can confuse the process. A prompt can be as small as one word. With fewer details you get more variety; with more details you get more control.","sources":[{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Prompt Basics","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/prompts"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The docs give an example. A long, chatty request for blooming California poppies in bright orange, drawn with colored pencils, becomes one plain line.","sources":[{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Prompt Basics","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/prompts"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: The short version","text":"Colored pencil illustration of bright orange California poppies","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Choose exact words and numbers","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Word choice matters. The docs recommend specific synonyms over generic ones, such as huge or enormous instead of big. Numbers matter even more. A plural like cats leaves the count up to Midjourney. Three cats, or a collective noun like a flock of birds, makes the result predictable.","sources":[{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Prompt Basics","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/prompts"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Say how many","text":"Three cats asleep on a sunny windowsill, soft morning light","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Add only the details you care about","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"When certain parts of the image matter to you, name them. Midjourney's docs list seven areas to think about: subject (a person, animal, object or place), medium (photo, painting, illustration, sculpture, doodle), environment (indoors, underwater, in the city), lighting (soft, overcast, studio, neon), color (vibrant, muted, pastel, black and white), mood (calm, playful, gloomy, energetic) and composition (portrait, headshot, closeup, bird's-eye view).","sources":[{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Prompt Basics","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/prompts"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"You do not need all seven. Pick the two or three that decide whether the image works for you, and let Midjourney's default style handle the rest.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: A detailed photo","text":"Closeup photo of [subject] [doing something] in [place], [lighting] light, [color] colors, [mood] mood","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Put parameters at the end","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Parameters are settings you type after the description. Midjourney's parameter list says they go at the end of the prompt, with a space before the two dashes and no commas or periods inside them. The most useful ones for beginners are --ar to change the shape of the image, --s (stylize) to control how much of Midjourney's own artistic style is applied, --chaos to get more varied results, and --raw for more control over the output.","sources":[{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Parameter List","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/parameter-list"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"For the current V8.1 model, a third-party prompt guide from Evolink lists the defaults: square 1:1 images, stylize at 100 on a scale of 0 to 1000, and chaos at 0 on a scale of 0 to 100. Stylize sets how strongly Midjourney's default look is applied, so lower values give a plainer result.","sources":[{"name":"Evolink: Midjourney V8.1 prompt guide","url":"https://evolink.ai/docs/en/api-manual/image-series/midjourney/midjourney-v8-1-prompt-guide"},{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Parameter List","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/parameter-list"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: A wide image with a bit more style","text":"Watercolor painting of a lighthouse on a cliff at sunset --ar 16:9 --s 250","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Use --ar 4:5 or --ar 9:16 for images meant for a phone screen, and --ar 16:9 for slides and desktop wallpapers.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Say what you want, not what you do not want","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"This is the mistake most people make. If you write a party with no cake, the docs warn, you may still get a cake, because mentioning a thing can pull it into the image. Describe the scene you want instead. When you really need to remove something, use the --no parameter, which Midjourney's parameter list describes as the way to exclude elements from an image.","sources":[{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Prompt Basics","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/prompts"},{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Parameter List","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/parameter-list"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: Remove an object","text":"Minimal living room with a gray sofa and tall windows --no plants","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Pick the right model","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Midjourney's Models page lists V6, V6.1, V7 and V8.1, plus Niji 7 for anime and illustration. You can choose one for a single image by adding --v and the number at the end, for example --v 8.1, or set a default in the settings panel. V8.1 renders standard jobs several times faster than earlier versions, holds on to small details and can make 2K images with --hd. It does not support some older features, including Character Reference and Omni Reference.","sources":[{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Models","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/models"},{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Parameter List","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/parameter-list"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Testers report that newer models want clearer direction. Heather Cooper, who writes the Visually AI newsletter, found that V8 rewards more detail than V7 did, and she recommends switching to --raw for controlled or photorealistic results. Midjourney's docs say the same about Raw: it removes default styling for stronger prompt adherence.","sources":[{"name":"Visually AI (Heather Cooper): Midjourney V8 is live on alpha","url":"https://heatherbcooper.substack.com/p/midjourney-v8-is-live-on-alpha-heres"},{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Models","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/models"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Write the core line","text":"Describe the subject and the medium in one short sentence, such as a photo of a red bicycle against a white wall.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Add two or three details","text":"Choose the lighting, mood or composition that matters most to you. Stop there.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Add parameters","text":"Set the shape with --ar, and add --raw if the result looks too stylized.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Change one thing at a time","text":"If the image is not right, change a single word or setting and run it again, so you know what made the difference.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 6: Text inside the image","text":"Vintage travel poster for a mountain town with the words \"Visit Alpine Falls\" --v 8.1","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"For words inside an image, put the exact text in quotation marks. Cooper reports that V8 renders quoted text with higher accuracy.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Midjourney is good at mood, lighting and style, and a short prompt often gives a more striking result than a long one. It is weaker when you need exact control over many objects at once, and results still vary from run to run. Treat the first set of four images as a draft, keep the version you like, and refine from there.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: GitHub Copilot is free in VS Code. 5 steps to make it write, explain and fix your code
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: In VS Code, hover over the Copilot icon in the Status Bar, pick Use AI Features and sign in with GitHub. No plan yet? Signing in puts you on Copilot Free: 2,000 completions a month plus AI credits. Sources: GitHub Docs: Plans for GitHub Copilot, GitHub Docs: Quickstart for GitHub Copilot in your IDE, VS Code Docs: Set up GitHub Copilot, VS Code Docs: Inline suggestions from GitHub Copilot, VS Code Docs: GitHub Copilot cheat sheet, VS Code Docs: Complete your first task with an agent, VS Code Docs: Custom instructions, Fast.io: How to use GitHub Copilot.
