item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM): how to turn your documents into notes, quizzes and audio","dek":"How to set up a notebook, ask questions about your own files, and use Audio Overviews, flashcards, quizzes and reports, with prompts to copy.","summary":"Google renamed NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook on July 16, 2026, but it still works the same way: you add your own sources and it answers and builds study material from them. Here is how to use each part, step by step, and where it falls short.","seo_title":"Gemini Notebook (NotebookLM) Guide: Notes, Quizzes, Audio","seo_description":"How to use Gemini Notebook, formerly NotebookLM: add sources, ask cited questions, make Audio Overviews, flashcards, quizzes and study guides.","answer_summary":"Create a notebook, add your sources (PDFs, Docs, slides, audio, links or YouTube videos), ask questions in the chat, then use the Studio panel to generate Audio Overviews, flashcards, quizzes, reports and more from those sources.","tags":["Gemini Notebook","NotebookLM","Google","Studying","AI guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Gemini Notebook is the new name for NotebookLM, Google's research and study tool. Google announced the rename on July 16, 2026, and said the product stays a standalone research tool. The idea has not changed: you give it your own material, such as lecture notes, PDFs or a recorded talk, and it answers questions and builds study aids from that material instead of from the open web. This guide covers how to set up a notebook, how to ask good questions, and how to use Audio Overviews, flashcards, quizzes and reports.","sources":[{"name":"Google: NotebookLM is now Gemini Notebook","url":"https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/products/gemini-notebook/notebooklm-gemini-notebook/"},{"name":"Google Workspace Updates","url":"https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2026/07/notebooklm-now-gemini-notebook.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"If you used NotebookLM before, nothing breaks. Google's Workspace team said automatic redirects keep existing shared notebooks and links working, and the new name and logo appear across the product over several weeks. On mobile you may need to update the app.","sources":[{"name":"Google Workspace Updates","url":"https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2026/07/notebooklm-now-gemini-notebook.html"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Set up your first notebook","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Create a notebook","text":"Open Gemini Notebook in your browser and select Create new notebook. In the window that opens, choose Upload a source. Use one notebook per subject or project. Each notebook is separate, and Gemini Notebook cannot pull information from several notebooks at once, so a notebook for your biology class will not know what is in your history notebook.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Add the right sources","text":"Select Add sources on the left. Gemini Notebook accepts PDFs, Google Docs, Google Slides, Google Sheets, Word, PowerPoint, TXT, Markdown, CSV and ePub files, images, audio files such as MP3 and WAV, pasted text, web links, public YouTube videos and Gemini chats. Each source can hold up to 500,000 words, or 200 MB for an uploaded file, and free users can add up to 50 sources per notebook. Sources from Google Drive sync automatically, but footnotes and comments in those files are not imported.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"No material yet: type a question into the search box in the Sources panel and pick Web or Drive. Gemini Notebook shows results you can import. Turn on Deep Research for a longer search that takes a few minutes; Google says that option is only for users over 18.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Ask questions about your own files","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Once sources are in, the chat panel shows a summary of them and suggested questions. Answers draw on the notebook's sources and include citations that link back to the passage they came from, according to Layer3Labs' walkthrough. You can also switch individual sources off in the Sources panel to narrow what an answer uses.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Create a notebook","url":"https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16206563?hl=en"},{"name":"Layer3Labs","url":"https://www.layer3labs.io/guides/how-to-use-notebooklm"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Find what matters for the test","text":"Using only my sources, explain [topic] in plain words. Then list the 5 facts I am most likely to be tested on, and point to where each one appears.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Spot the gaps","text":"Compare what [source 1] and [source 2] say about [topic]. List where they agree, where they disagree, and anything one covers that the other leaves out.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Click the citations on anything you plan to quote or memorize. The answer is only as good as the passage behind it, and checking takes seconds.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Turn your notes into a podcast","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Audio Overviews live in the Studio panel. Google's help center lists four formats: Deep Dive, the default, where two hosts discuss your sources; The Brief, one speaker giving the key points in under two minutes; The Critique, two hosts giving feedback on something like an essay; and The Debate, two hosts arguing different sides. You can choose Shorter, Default or Longer, though Longer works in English only. More than 80 languages are supported.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Generate Audio Overview","url":"https://support.google.com/notebooklm/answer/16212820?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Generate an Audio Overview with a focus","text":"In Studio, open Audio Overview, pick a format and length, and add a prompt that says what to focus on and how expert the listener is. It generates in the background, which can take a couple of minutes, so you can keep working. You can download the audio when it is done.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: A beginner's audio lesson","text":"Focus only on [chapter or topic]. Explain it for a beginner, use one everyday example per idea, and end with the 3 points I must remember.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"There is also an Interactive mode. When you create a new Audio Overview with it switched on, you can select Join while listening and ask the hosts a question by voice; they answer from your sources and then carry on. Google says it is English only, works only on newly generated overviews, and may have delays or audio glitches.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Generate Audio Overview","url":"https://support.google.com/notebooklm/answer/16212820?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Quiz yourself with flashcards and quizzes","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Customize before you generate","text":"In Studio, select Flashcards or Quizzes to generate right away, or click the pencil icon first to customize. You can set the difficulty to easy, medium or hard, choose fewer, standard or more items, and add a prompt about the topic, audience or style.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Questions that test understanding","text":"Make questions only about [topic]. Mix definitions with questions that ask me to apply an idea to a new example. Skip anything not in my sources.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"While you study, the Explain button gives the reasoning behind a card or an answer. On flashcards you mark each card Got it! or Missed it!, and Gemini Notebook saves your progress. At the end you can practice again with the same cards, all cards, or only the ones you missed. Flashcards can be downloaded as a CSV file.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Generate Flashcards or Quizzes","url":"https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16958963"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Build study guides and reports","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The Studio panel also makes notes, Video Overviews, mind maps, data tables, slide decks, infographics and reports. Report types include a study guide, a briefing document, an FAQ or a custom report, and a report can be exported to Google Docs from its three dot menu. Edits you make in the exported Doc do not sync back to the notebook.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Notebook Help: Create a notebook","url":"https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16206563?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: A one page study guide","text":"Create a one page study guide on [topic]: key terms with short definitions, a timeline of the main events, and 5 practice questions with answers.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What it is bad at","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Gemini Notebook is only as good as what you put in. If your sources are thin or wrong, its answers and quizzes will be too, and it will not tell you what your notes are missing unless you ask. Google itself warns that Audio Overviews are AI generated and can contain inaccuracies, so treat them as a way to review, not as the final word. It also cannot combine notebooks, and the mobile app may not support every feature. For a quick fact check against the open web, a search tool is still the better fit; for learning a specific set of material well, this is the tool to use.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Free accounts get the core features. Google's paid AI plans raise the limits on notebooks, sources and daily generations, and some newer features, such as code that runs inside a notebook to analyze data, started with Google AI Ultra users before a wider rollout.","sources":[{"name":"Google: NotebookLM is now Gemini Notebook","url":"https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/products/gemini-notebook/notebooklm-gemini-notebook/"},{"name":"Layer3Labs","url":"https://www.layer3labs.io/guides/how-to-use-notebooklm"}]}]}

item.title: You're using Perplexity like Google. 4 habits turn it into a real research assistant
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: undefined... Sources: Perplexity Help Center: What is Research mode?, Perplexity Help Center: What are Projects?, Perplexity: How does Perplexity work?, Fast Company, Dupple, Fello AI.
item.category: Perplexity Help Center: What is Research mode?
Perplexity Help Center: What are Projects?

nf:hero.nf:alt: A young woman holding a laptop at a library table covered in stacks of books, with the Perplexity logo on the wall.

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"Perplexity: how to research with sources you can actually check","dek":"How to ask better questions, choose where Perplexity searches, verify its citations, and use Research mode and Projects for bigger jobs.","summary":"Perplexity searches the web and answers with numbered citations, but the answer is only as good as the question and the sources behind it. Here is how to set up each step, which features need a paid plan, and where Perplexity falls short.","seo_title":"Perplexity Guide: How to Research With Sources","seo_description":"How to use Perplexity for research: narrow questions, the sources menu, checking citations, Research mode and Projects, with copy and paste prompts.","answer_summary":"Ask a specific question, choose the right sources (Web, Academic, Social or Finance), click the numbered citations to check each claim, and select Research in the mode selector when you need a full cited report.","tags":["Perplexity","AI search","Research","AI guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Perplexity is an AI search engine. You type a question, it searches the web in real time, and it writes an answer with numbered footnotes that link to the pages it used. That last part is what makes it useful for research: you can check every claim. The catch is that most people read the answer and never open a single source. This guide covers how to ask, how to pick sources, how to check the citations, and when to use Research mode and Projects.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity: How does Perplexity work?","url":"https://hub-prod.perplexity.ai/hub/faq/how-does-perplexity-work"},{"name":"Fast Company","url":"https://www.fastcompany.com/91367673/perplexity-tips"},{"name":"Dupple","url":"https://dupple.com/learn/how-to-use-perplexity-ai"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Start with a narrow question","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Perplexity handles plain, conversational questions, but specific questions get better answers. Fast Company gives a simple example: a query for the latest breakthroughs in EV battery recycling methods works better than just typing EV batteries. Answers also keep context inside a thread, so you can ask a follow up without repeating the whole question.","sources":[{"name":"Fast Company","url":"https://www.fastcompany.com/91367673/perplexity-tips"},{"name":"Dupple","url":"https://dupple.com/learn/how-to-use-perplexity-ai"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Name the topic, the time frame and the output","text":"Say what you want to know, which period it covers, and what shape the answer should take: a list, a comparison, a short summary. If dates matter, ask for the date of each source so you can see how fresh the information is.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: What changed recently","text":"What changed in [topic] between [month, year] and today? Use only sources published in that period, list the 3 most important changes, and give the date of each source.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Keep digging in the same thread","text":"Ask your follow ups as replies in the same thread instead of starting a new search. Perplexity keeps the earlier questions in context, so you can go from a broad overview to one specific detail in a few steps.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Choose where it searches","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The search box has a sources menu that sets where Perplexity looks. Web is the default and covers news, current events and popular sites. Academic leans on scientific papers, scholarly articles and research journals. Social pulls in discussions and firsthand experiences from people, and Finance focuses on market data, company reports and investment news, according to Fast Company.","sources":[{"name":"Fast Company","url":"https://www.fastcompany.com/91367673/perplexity-tips"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Switch to Academic for health, science and research questions","text":"When the question is about evidence, not opinion, set the sources to Academic before you search. Then ask Perplexity to separate strong findings from early ones.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: What the studies say","text":"Summarize what peer reviewed studies say about [question]. Separate strong evidence from early or small studies, and say where the studies disagree.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Use Social when you want real experiences, like how owners feel about a product after a year. Treat those answers as opinions, not facts.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Check the citations","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Each answer has numbered citations, and clicking one opens the original page. Dupple's guide warns that the AI can still get things wrong and recommends clicking through to verify claims, especially statistics. Fast Company makes the same point: the citations exist so you can read the summary in its original context.","sources":[{"name":"Fast Company","url":"https://www.fastcompany.com/91367673/perplexity-tips"},{"name":"Dupple","url":"https://dupple.com/learn/how-to-use-perplexity-ai"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Ask which source supports which claim","text":"After a long answer, ask Perplexity to map each claim to its source. Then open the sources for the claims you plan to use, and read the sentence yourself. If a number is not on the page, do not use it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Show your work","text":"For each claim in your last answer, tell me which numbered source supports it. Flag any claim that no source directly supports.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Use Research mode for the big questions","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Research mode is Perplexity's deeper option. According to its help center, it runs many searches, reads a large number of sources and reasons through them to write a full report. You turn it on by selecting Research from the mode selector in the search box, on the web, the mobile apps and the Mac app. Most tasks finish in under 3 minutes, but some take 4 to 5 minutes.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: What is Research mode?","url":"https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/10738684-what-is-research-mode"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Free users get limited access to Research mode and Pro subscribers get extended access. Limits reset on a rolling basis, not on a fixed date. You cannot pick the model in Research mode; Perplexity chooses it. When the report is done, you can export it as a PDF or a document, or turn it into a Perplexity Page to share.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: What is Research mode?","url":"https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/10738684-what-is-research-mode"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: A full report","text":"Write a research report on [topic] for [who it is for]. Cover [point 1], [point 2] and [point 3], end with a short list of open questions, and cite a source for every number.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"For quick everyday questions, the faster standard search is enough. Perplexity describes Pro Search as the deeper option for complex questions: it may ask you follow up questions to refine what you want, and free accounts get a limited number of Pro Searches.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity: How does Perplexity work?","url":"https://hub-prod.perplexity.ai/hub/faq/how-does-perplexity-work"},{"name":"Fast Company","url":"https://www.fastcompany.com/91367673/perplexity-tips"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Keep long research in a Project","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Projects are the new name for what Perplexity used to call Spaces; the company renamed them on July 30, 2026, according to Fello AI. A Project keeps searches, files, instructions and connected tools in one place, so you can return to the same research over time.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: What are Projects?","url":"https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/10352961-what-are-projects"},{"name":"Fello AI","url":"https://felloai.com/perplexity-spaces/"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Create a Project","text":"Open the Projects section in the left sidebar and select New project. Give it a title of up to 50 characters. You can add a description, an icon and a color.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Add instructions and files","text":"In the Project settings, add instructions of up to 8,000 characters. They apply to every query you run in that Project, so this is where you put your preferred format or the kinds of sources you trust. Then upload files or whole folders.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The help center lists the same file limits on every plan: up to 10,000 files and 5 GB per Project, with each file up to 100 MB. On personal accounts a Project is visible only to people you give access to, and you can add up to 5 contributors.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: What are Projects?","url":"https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/10352961-what-are-projects"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where Perplexity falls short","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Perplexity is a research shortcut, not a replacement for reading. A summary can flatten a nuance, mix up two sources, or attach a number to the wrong page. The citations make those mistakes easy to catch, but only if you open them.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"It is also not the best tool for every search. Dupple notes that Google is still better for going straight to a specific website or finding a local business. Several features, including more Pro Searches and file uploads, are tied to the paid Pro plan, which both Fast Company and Dupple list at $20 a month.","sources":[{"name":"Fast Company","url":"https://www.fastcompany.com/91367673/perplexity-tips"},{"name":"Dupple","url":"https://dupple.com/learn/how-to-use-perplexity-ai"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Before you share anything Perplexity wrote, open at least the sources behind the numbers. If you cannot find the claim on the page, leave it out.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Most people use Gemini like a search box. These 4 features make it work for you
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: A Gem is Gemini with your instructions saved. On gemini.google.com click Explore Gems, then New Gem. It is free on every plan. You make it on the web, then use it on your phone too. Preview it on the right before you click Save. Click Add files under the chat box, then Upload or Add from Drive. Up to 10 files per prompt. Sources: Gemini Apps Help: Get started with Gems, Gemini Apps Help: Upload and analyze files, Gemini Apps Help: Google Workspace app, Zapier: Gemini Gems, Zapier: Gemini connected apps, Chrome Story.
item.category: Gemini Apps Help: Get started with Gems
Gemini Apps Help: Upload and analyze files
Gemini Apps Help: Google Workspace app

nf:hero.nf:alt: An office worker holding a laptop in a cluttered office full of paper stacks, with the Gemini logo on the wall.

item.nf:article:
{"kind":"guide","headline":"Gemini: a practical guide to Gems, file uploads and Gmail and Drive","dek":"How to build a Gem that remembers your instructions, what Gemini can do with your files, and how to let it search your own Google Workspace.","summary":"Gems, file uploads and the Google Workspace connection are the three Gemini features that matter most for everyday work. Here is how to set up each one, the current limits, and where each one falls short.","seo_title":"Gemini Guide: Gems, File Uploads, Gmail and Drive","seo_description":"How to create Gemini Gems, write instructions, upload files and connect Gmail, Drive and Calendar, with copy and paste prompts and the current limits.","answer_summary":"Create a Gem on gemini.google.com with Explore Gems and New Gem, upload files with the Add files button (up to 10 per prompt), and connect Google Workspace so you can ask about your Gmail, Drive, Docs and Calendar.","tags":["Gemini","Google","Gemini Gems","Google Workspace","AI guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Most people open Gemini, type a question and close the tab. Three features change that: Gems, which save your instructions so you stop repeating them, file uploads, which let Gemini read your documents, videos and code, and the Google Workspace connection, which lets it search your own Gmail, Drive, Docs and Calendar. All three are documented in Google's Gemini Apps Help pages. This guide covers how to set up each one, the limits Google lists, and where each one falls short.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Get started with Gems","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/15235603"},{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Upload and analyze files","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/14903178"},{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Google Workspace app","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/15229592?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Gems: set your instructions once","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"A Gem is a saved version of Gemini with your own instructions about goals, behavior and output format. Zapier compares Gems to custom GPTs in ChatGPT: you set them up once and reuse them every time. Chrome Story reports that Gems are free on every Gemini plan, including the free tier, so you do not need Google AI Pro or Ultra to make one.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Get started with Gems","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/15235603"},{"name":"Zapier: Gemini Gems","url":"https://zapier.com/blog/gemini-gems/"},{"name":"Chrome Story","url":"https://chromestory.com/2026/07/create-gem-gemini-app/"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Open the Gem builder","text":"Go to gemini.google.com on a computer and sign in. In the panel on the left, click Explore Gems, then New Gem. Gems can only be created and edited in the web app. Once saved, they also show up in the Gemini mobile app, where you can chat with them.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Name it and write the instructions","text":"Give the Gem a short name you will recognize in a list, such as Email editor or Trip planner. Then write the instructions. Google suggests covering up to four things: the persona (the role the Gem plays), the task (what it should do), the context (background, as much as you can give) and the format (how the answer should look). You do not need all four.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: A starting template for any Gem","text":"You are my [role, for example email editor].
Your task is to [what you want done every time].
Context: [who I am, who the audience is, anything it should always know].
Format: [for example bullet points, under 150 words, plain language].
If anything in my request is unclear, ask me one question before you answer.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If writing instructions feels like work, type one or two sentences about your goal into the instructions box and use the Use Gemini to re-write instructions option. It expands your draft into fuller instructions. Read the result and cut anything you did not mean before you save.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Add knowledge files","text":"Under Knowledge, click Add files, then choose Upload files for something on your computer or Drive for a file in Google Drive. A style guide, a price list or a set of past examples works well here. If you do not want the Gem to cite these files in its answers, select Disable knowledge citations.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Preview, then save","text":"Type a test request in the preview panel on the right. The preview does not save anything, so adjust the instructions until the answers look right, then click Save. To change a Gem later, open your Gems list and click the pencil icon next to it. The three dot menu has Make a copy, which also works on Google's premade Gems.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: A writing editor Gem","text":"You are a careful editor for [my newsletter / my work emails].
When I paste a draft, fix grammar and spelling, cut filler words and keep my voice.
Do not add new facts or change numbers.
Return the edited text first, then a short list of the three biggest changes you made.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Gems have real limits. According to Zapier, they cannot be used with Gemini Live, they do not take actions outside the chat window, and they cannot use connected apps. So a Gem is best for repeated writing, editing and planning tasks, not for anything that needs your inbox or calendar.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"File uploads: what Gemini can read","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"In the Gemini web app, click the Add files button below the text box. Upload takes a file from your device and Add from Drive takes one from Google Drive. Under More Uploads you can also import a code folder or a GitHub repository. According to Google, most file types are supported and you can add up to 10 files in the same prompt. Videos can be up to 2 GB each and most other files up to 100 MB.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Upload and analyze files","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/14903178"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Length limits depend on the plan. Google says the total video length is up to 5 minutes, or up to 1 hour with Google AI Pro or Ultra, and the total audio length is up to 10 minutes, or up to 3 hours on those plans. One code folder or GitHub repository can be added per chat, with up to 5,000 files and 100 MB. Upload limits are rolling, so if you hit one, you may have to wait before uploading more.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Upload and analyze files","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/14903178"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Get the useful part of a long PDF","text":"Read the attached file.
1. Summarize it in five bullet points.
2. List every deadline, date and number that I need to act on, with the page it appears on.
3. Tell me what is missing or unclear.
Only use what is in the file. If something is not in it, say so.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Google warns that very large uploads can lead to answers that miss details or connections across the content. If you need precise answers, upload fewer files at once and ask about one document at a time. If Gemini clearly misreads a file, upload it again.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Gmail, Drive and Calendar: ask about your own stuff","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The Google Workspace app connects Gemini to your Gmail, Docs and Drive for summaries and lookups, to Google Tasks and Google Keep for reminders, notes and lists, and to Google Calendar for events. To point Gemini at one service, type @ and pick it from the list. Google says to use keywords from the content rather than pasting a link to an email or a document.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Google Workspace app","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/15229592?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Connect Google Workspace","text":"Sign in to Gemini with the same account you use for Gmail and Drive. Keep Activity must be on, or Gemini cannot connect. In Gmail, the setting Smart features in other Google products also has to be on; after you turn it on, reload Gemini. Work and school accounts need the administrator to allow the connection first. To disconnect later, use the Connected Apps settings page.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Clear your inbox backlog","text":"@Gmail Find emails from the last 7 days that ask me to reply, decide or send something.
For each one, give me the sender, what they need and by when.
Sort them by deadline, soonest first.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: Prepare for a meeting","text":"@Google Calendar What is my next meeting with [name]?
@Drive Find the latest documents that mention [project].
Give me a five line briefing: what the meeting is about, what changed since we last met, and two questions I should ask.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The limits matter here. Google lists them plainly: Gemini cannot see comments or images inside Docs and Gmail, or pictures and videos in Drive. It cannot create folders or move files in Drive, cannot count items in Drive or Gmail, and cannot report your storage. In a new chat, name the service in your first prompt; follow up questions in the same chat do not need it. Zapier adds that the list of connected apps and their availability varies by country.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Google Workspace app","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/15229592?hl=en"},{"name":"Zapier: Gemini connected apps","url":"https://zapier.com/blog/gemini-connected-apps/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The Workspace connection is the most useful of the three for busy people, and also the one that needs the most checking. Google itself notes that Gemini can hallucinate or give outdated information here, so open the emails and files it cites before you act on a summary.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where to start","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Start with one Gem for the task you repeat most, such as editing emails. Use uploads when you have one long document to understand. Turn on the Workspace connection when you spend too long searching your own inbox, and always check the sources it shows.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Stop pasting the same files into Claude. 3 features that do the work for you
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: A project is a workspace with its own chats, files and instructions. Free accounts can make up to five. Add your reference files once and every chat in that project can use them. Start chats from inside the project, not the main sidebar. Click + in the chat box, then Add files or photos. PDFs, Word files, CSVs, spreadsheets and images all work. Sources: Claude Help Center: What are projects, Claude Help Center: RAG for projects, Claude Help Center: Uploading files, Claude Help Center: Artifacts, Claude: Artifacts, Ascendient Learning, Maginative, Developers Digest, Kevin Stratvert.
item.category: Claude Help Center: What are projects
Claude Help Center: RAG for projects

nf:hero.nf:alt: Stop pasting the same files into Claude. 3 features that do the work for you

item.nf:article:
{"kind":"guide","headline":"Claude Projects, file uploads and artifacts: a practical guide","dek":"How to set up a Claude project, write instructions that stick, get the most from uploaded files and turn answers into documents and tools.","summary":"Projects, file uploads and artifacts are the three Claude features that matter most for everyday work. Here is how to set up each one, what the limits are and where each one falls short.","seo_title":"Claude Projects, Files and Artifacts: A Practical Guide","seo_description":"How to set up Claude Projects, write project instructions, upload PDFs and spreadsheets, and create artifacts, with copy and paste prompts and current limits.","answer_summary":"Create a project, add instructions and reference files once, start every chat from inside it, upload files with the + button in the chat box, and ask Claude for a document, deck or tool to get an artifact beside the chat.","tags":["Claude","Anthropic","Claude Projects","Artifacts","AI guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"If you use Claude for the same kind of work every week, three features save the most time: Projects, file uploads and artifacts. Projects are self-contained workspaces with their own chat history and knowledge base, according to Anthropic's help center. File uploads let Claude read your PDFs, documents, spreadsheets and images. Artifacts are the documents, decks, dashboards and small tools Claude builds in a panel beside the conversation. This guide covers how to set up each one, the limits that apply and where each one falls short.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: What are projects","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9517075-what-are-projects"},{"name":"Claude Help Center: Uploading files","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8241126-uploading-files-to-claude"},{"name":"Claude Help Center: Artifacts","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9487310-what-are-artifacts-and-how-do-i-use-them"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Projects: set the context once","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Anthropic says Projects are available to every user, including free accounts, and that free users can create up to five projects. Each project has a knowledge base, where you add documents, text and code, and a set of instructions that shape how Claude answers inside it, such as a more formal tone or the point of view of a specific role.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: What are projects","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9517075-what-are-projects"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Create the project","text":"Go to Projects and create a new one. Give it a name you will recognize later, like the client, the class or the report. According to Ascendient Learning, Claude does not read the project name or description; they are only there to help you stay organized.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Write the instructions","text":"Open the project's instructions and write the brief you would otherwise paste into every chat. Ascendient Learning notes the instructions are added at the start of every conversation in the project. Say who Claude is helping, who the audience is, the format you want, the tone and where the facts come from.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Project instructions starter","text":"You are helping me with [project name]. The audience is [who will read the work].
Write in a [tone] tone. Keep answers under [length] unless I ask for more.
Use the files in this project as your main source. If something is not in the files, say so instead of guessing.
When I ask for a draft, give me one version first, then a short list of what you would change.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Add your reference files","text":"Upload the material the work depends on, such as a brief, a style guide, a plan or last quarter's numbers, to the project's files. Once they are there, every chat in the project can use them, so you do not upload the same document again.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Start chats from inside the project","text":"Open the project and start a new chat there. Ascendient Learning points out that a chat started from the main sidebar has no project context, which is the most common reason people think their instructions are being ignored.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"On paid plans (Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise), a project can hold more material than fits in Claude's context window. When the knowledge base gets close to that limit, Claude switches to retrieval mode, which Anthropic says can expand capacity by up to 10 times. It turns on automatically and the project shows an indicator when it is active. Anthropic recommends clear, descriptive file names and naming the document you mean in your question.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: RAG for projects","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11473015-retrieval-augmented-generation-rag-for-projects"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"On Team and Enterprise plans, projects can be shared with colleagues, who can be given view or edit access. Free, Pro and Max accounts do not get project sharing, according to the help center.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: What are projects","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9517075-what-are-projects"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Keep one project per piece of work, not one giant project for everything. Smaller projects keep Claude focused on the right files and make the instructions easier to get right.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"File uploads: what Claude can read","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Claude accepts PDF, DOCX, CSV, TXT, HTML, ODT, RTF, EPUB, JSON and XLSX documents, plus JPEG, PNG, GIF and WebP images. Spreadsheets in XLSX format need the code execution and file creation setting turned on. To upload, click the + button in the lower left of the chat box and choose Add files or photos, or drag files into the window. You can also paste an image from your clipboard.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: Uploading files","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8241126-uploading-files-to-claude"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"In a single chat, the limits are 500 MB per file, up to 20 files, images up to 8000 by 8000 pixels and PDFs up to 1,000 pages. For PDFs of 100 pages or fewer, Claude also analyzes charts, images and graphics. Longer PDFs are read as text only. Other document types are read for text only, so Claude will not see images embedded in a Word file. Files added to a project have a 30 MB limit per file.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: Uploading files","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8241126-uploading-files-to-claude"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Get the key points out of a long PDF","text":"Read the attached PDF. Give me:
1. A five-sentence summary.
2. Every date, deadline and number that matters, in a table with the page number for each.
3. Anything that looks unclear or contradictory.
Use the page numbers shown in my PDF viewer.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"When you point Claude to a page, use the page number your PDF viewer shows, not the number printed on the page. Anthropic recommends this because the two often differ. If a file is too big, split it into sections.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Check a spreadsheet before you send it","text":"Look at the attached spreadsheet. Tell me which columns have missing values, which numbers look out of range compared with the rest of the column, and any totals that do not add up. Then suggest three charts that would explain this data to [audience].","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Artifacts: from answer to finished work","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"An artifact is a standalone piece of work, such as a document, a slide deck, a design, a dashboard or a small interactive tool, that opens in its own window beside the chat. Anthropic says Claude creates one when the content is substantial, self-contained and likely to be edited or reused. You can ask for one in the chat, pick Output in the message box, or start from the Artifacts tab, where everything you create is saved.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: Artifacts","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9487310-what-are-artifacts-and-how-do-i-use-them"},{"name":"Claude: Artifacts","url":"https://claude.com/features/artifacts"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Turn on the setting","text":"Artifacts need Cloud code execution and file creation. On Free, Pro and Max, it is under Settings, Capabilities. On Team and Enterprise, an owner turns it on in the organization settings.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Ask for the output, not just an answer","text":"Be specific about the format: a one-page document, a ten-slide deck or a simple calculator. Then ask for changes in the chat, or edit a template artifact directly, for example by typing in a doc or changing a slide.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Fix and share","text":"If an artifact shows an error, use Try fixing with Claude near the error. Artifacts start private, and you choose when to share them.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Anthropic's help center lists Docs, Slides and Design templates as a beta for paid plans. Docs export to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, and Slides export to PowerPoint or PDF. Artifacts can also call Claude themselves, which lets them work as small apps, and each person who uses a shared one does so with their own account and plan limits.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: Artifacts","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9487310-what-are-artifacts-and-how-do-i-use-them"},{"name":"Developers Digest","url":"https://www.developersdigest.tech/blog/claude-design-slides-and-docs"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Turn notes into a shareable document","text":"Turn my notes below into a one-page document for [audience]. Use a short title, three sections with headings, and a final list of next steps with an owner for each. Keep it under 400 words.

[paste your notes]","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where these features fall short","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Projects only help if you start chats inside them, and the five-project cap on free accounts fills up fast. Non-PDF documents lose their images, and long PDFs lose their charts, so a chart buried in a Word file or on page 300 of a report will be missed. Artifacts are good for drafts and simple tools, but they still need a human check before anything goes out. Treat a published artifact from someone you do not know with the same caution as a file from an unknown sender, which is what Anthropic advises.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Stop using ChatGPT like a search box. 4 features that make it work for you
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Open Projects in the left menu, name it, then add files, instructions or old chats. Everything inside carries over to every new chat in that project, so you stop repeating yourself. Plus gets 20 files per project, Pro 40. Say it plainly: "Remember that I'm vegetarian when you suggest recipes." Saved memories stay even if you delete the chat. Ask ChatGPT to forget something, or manage it all in Settings. Sources: OpenAI Academy: Projects, OpenAI Help: Memory FAQ, OpenAI Help: File Uploads FAQ, OpenAI Academy: Working with files, Unite.AI, DataCamp.

nf:hero.nf:alt: A person at a cluttered table working on a laptop, with the OpenAI logo on the wall behind.

item.nf:article:
{"kind":"guide","headline":"ChatGPT for everyday work: how to use Projects, memory and file uploads","dek":"Set up Projects, control what ChatGPT remembers, use Temporary Chat and get real work out of your PDFs and spreadsheets.","summary":"Projects, memory, Temporary Chat and file uploads turn ChatGPT into a work tool. Here is how to set up each one, with copy and paste prompts and the limits that apply on each plan.","seo_title":"ChatGPT Projects, Memory and File Uploads: A Practical Guide","seo_description":"How to set up ChatGPT Projects, manage memory, use Temporary Chat and upload files, with copy and paste prompts and current limits.","answer_summary":"Create a project from the left menu, add instructions and files, tell ChatGPT what to remember in plain words, use Temporary Chat for one-off questions, and attach files from the tools menu with a specific request.","tags":["ChatGPT","OpenAI","ChatGPT Projects","AI guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Four ChatGPT features do most of the heavy lifting for everyday work: Projects, memory, Temporary Chat and file uploads. Projects keep the files, instructions and chats for one piece of work together. Memory lets ChatGPT keep details you want it to know. Temporary Chat keeps a conversation out of all of that. File uploads let it read your PDFs, documents, spreadsheets and images. This guide shows how to set up each one and when to skip it.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Academy: Projects","url":"https://openai.com/academy/projects"},{"name":"OpenAI Help: Memory FAQ","url":"https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq"},{"name":"OpenAI Help: File Uploads FAQ","url":"https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8555545-file-uploads-faq"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Projects: one place for one job","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenAI describes a project as a dedicated space for a body of work. Each project holds its own files and instructions, and they apply to every chat inside it, so you do not have to upload the same document or repeat the same background in each new conversation.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Academy: Projects","url":"https://openai.com/academy/projects"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Create the project","text":"Open Projects from the left-hand menu, create a new project and give it a name you will recognize later, such as the client, the class or the trip.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Add instructions","text":"Write the guidance you would otherwise paste into every chat: who you are, who the work is for, the tone you want, and what to avoid. Project instructions apply to the chats in that project and take priority over your general custom instructions there, according to Unite.AI.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Add files","text":"Upload the reference material the project depends on, like a brief, a style guide or last quarter's numbers. OpenAI's file FAQ lists project limits of 20 files on Plus and 40 files on Pro, Team, Education and Business plans.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Move old chats in","text":"If you already have conversations about the same work, move them into the project. DataCamp notes you can drag a chat into a project or add it from the chat's menu.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Some plans also offer project-only memory, which limits ChatGPT's context to conversations inside that same project. OpenAI says this helps keep projects separate. Unite.AI reported that the option is chosen when a project is created and cannot be switched on for an existing one, so decide before you start. On plans that support sharing, collaborators can work from the same files, instructions and history.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Academy: Projects","url":"https://openai.com/academy/projects"},{"name":"Unite.AI","url":"https://www.unite.ai/how-to-use-chatgpts-project-memory/"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Use a project for work that runs over days or weeks: research, a draft you revise in stages, recurring planning. For a quick, self-contained question, a normal chat is faster.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Write your project instructions","text":"You are helping me with [project name]. I am [your role], and the work is for [audience].
Always write in [tone] and keep answers under [length].
Use the files in this project as the main source. If something is not in the files, say so instead of guessing.
Before long answers, ask me one clarifying question if the request is unclear.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Memory: what ChatGPT keeps about you","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"ChatGPT has two kinds of memory, according to OpenAI's help center. Saved memories are details you ask it to keep, and they stay until you delete them, even if you delete the chat where they came up. Chat history lets ChatGPT draw on past conversations to learn your interests and preferences, and those details can change over time.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Help: Memory FAQ","url":"https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Save something on purpose","text":"Tell ChatGPT directly what to keep. A clear sentence with a reason works best, because it tells the model when the detail applies.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Save a useful memory","text":"Remember that I work in [industry] and write for [audience]. When I ask for emails or summaries, use plain American English and keep them under [number] words.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Check and clean it up","text":"Ask ChatGPT what it remembers about you. To remove a detail, ask it to forget it. OpenAI says a forgotten item can take a few days to stop being referenced, and the original conversation stays unless you delete it too.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Where the controls live depends on which memory system your account has. In the older system, saved memories are under Settings, then Personalization, where you can search them, delete single entries or delete all. OpenAI says a newer memory system is rolling out first to Plus and Pro users in the US, with its controls under Settings, then Memory. Turning off Reference saved memories also turns off Reference chat history. On Enterprise and Edu plans, workspace owners decide whether memory is on.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Help: Memory FAQ","url":"https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Audit your memory","text":"List everything you currently remember about me, grouped by topic. Mark anything that looks outdated or that you are unsure about, so I can tell you what to forget.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Temporary Chat: when you want a clean slate","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Temporary Chats do not appear in your chat history. In the new memory system, OpenAI says they also do not use your existing memories or create new ones. That makes them the right choice when you do not want a conversation to shape future answers.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Help: Memory FAQ","url":"https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Use Temporary Chat for a one-off question about a topic you do not want following you around, or to see how ChatGPT answers without your saved preferences. It is not a delete button for something you already said in a normal chat.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"File uploads: let ChatGPT read the document","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"7. Attach the file","text":"In a chat, open the tools menu and choose Add photos or files. OpenAI lists CSV, XLSX, PDF, DOCX, JPEG, PNG and TXT among the supported formats, and uploads work on the web and in the iOS and Android apps.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"8. Ask for something specific","text":"A file plus a vague request gets a vague answer. Say what you want back: a summary with risks, a table, a chart, or a rewrite. ChatGPT can also produce files you download, such as an updated spreadsheet.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Pull the facts out of a PDF","text":"Read the attached PDF. Make a table with these columns: date, what happens, who owns it, and the page it comes from. Then list any deadlines in the next [number] days.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: Make sense of a spreadsheet","text":"Look at the attached spreadsheet. Tell me in five bullet points what changed the most from [period] to [period], then make one chart that shows it. Explain any column you are not sure how to read.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The limits matter more than most people expect. OpenAI's file FAQ says free users get 3 file uploads per day, and everyone is limited to 80 files every 3 hours. Each file can be up to 512MB, images up to 20MB, and spreadsheets about 50MB depending on row size. Text documents are capped at 2 million tokens per file.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Help: File Uploads FAQ","url":"https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8555545-file-uploads-faq"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"There is one weakness to know about. Outside ChatGPT Enterprise, retrieval from PDFs is text-only, so images inside a document, such as charts or scanned pages, are discarded. Files you attach in a chat are kept as long as the chat exists and are deleted within 30 days after you delete the chat.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Help: File Uploads FAQ","url":"https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8555545-file-uploads-faq"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where these features fall short","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"None of this is perfect. Unite.AI reported that project memory works from short memory logs rather than every word of every chat, and that older entries can be replaced as memory fills up. DataCamp found that ChatGPT sometimes failed to find details from other chats in the same project. Deleting a memory also does not remove mentions in old chats, so OpenAI recommends deleting those chats as well.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Help: Memory FAQ","url":"https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq"},{"name":"Unite.AI","url":"https://www.unite.ai/how-to-use-chatgpts-project-memory/"},{"name":"DataCamp","url":"https://www.datacamp.com/blog/chatgpt-projects"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The practical takeaway is to put anything important in the project files or instructions, where ChatGPT sees it every time, instead of trusting it to recall a detail from an old conversation. Use memory for stable preferences, Temporary Chat for anything you would rather it forget, and always check figures it pulls from a file against the original.","sources":[]}]}
